ideas.expected_improvement: 0% in 300 s cells; avoids a projected −30-50% matched/s after about 10-15 min of sustained load, and caps the 1.3-6 GB RSS growth
ideas.risk: Dropped rows leave a gap in RPC trade history, which the writer's loss model already accepts after a crash (bg_writer.rs:7-10). It needs the gap marker and metric so the loss is visible. The projection is not observed directly: no current-build cell runs longer than 300 s. A 900 s cell would confirm it.
ideas.why_new: s64 records only 'queue mean 27, max 83' and proposes dropping low_pri. That fix makes the writer compete harder for CPU and does not bound the queue. Neither s64 nor the planned items note that the 256-batch cap turns a cosmetic writer into an exec stall after about 10 min, or the 24 MB-per-batch RSS cost.

ideas.title: Trade-history diet: compact primary rows plus a per-(user, block) aggregated user index, with rows built on the writer thread
ideas.area: torus-bridge native_executor.rs TradeKvs + torus-state bg_writer + torus-rpc torus.rs readers
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (1) The exec apply pass (native_executor.rs:4413-4417) hands over only a compact per-fill record (market u64, idx u32, maker, taker, price i128, qty i128, side), about 90 B instead of 297 B plus 3 row descriptors. (2) The writer thread builds: (a) a primary row key market|height|idx → price|qty|side|ts (41 B; drop the redundant u128 trade_id and height, which are already in the key); (b) ONE user-index row per (user, block), key addr|desc_block (28 B) → packed list of (market, idx, role) at about 13 B each. This goes in new CFs (e.g. cf_native_trades_v2 and cf_native_user_trades_v2) to avoid migrating old data. (3) get_user_trades (torus.rs:1674) prefix-scans the per-block lists and MultiGets the primary rows, at most 1000 per call. The WS scan is unchanged.
ideas.reasoning: Compaction cost here is dominated by entries, not bytes. 317 s of compaction CPU over roughly 67M trade rows plus about 1.4x rewrite is about 3.5 µs per entry. The writer's cost is dominated by per-row memtable skiplist inserts. So cutting rows matters most. Per block today: 58.6k fills × 3 = 175.8k rows and 17.4 MB. After the change: 58.6k primary rows plus at most 5k (user, block) rows (the bench has 5,000 senders) = 63.6k rows (−64%). Bytes: 58.6k × 61 B + 5k × 28 B + 117k × 13 B ≈ 5.2 MB (−70%). Applying about −60% to the trade-attributable CPU from idea 1 (writer about 1.2 cores, plus 60-85% of about 2.45 compaction cores, plus about 0.3 flush cores) frees about 1.8-2.2 host cores (10-12%). The trade share of WAL drops from 48% to about 15% of WAL bytes. The low-pri limiter throttles by bytes and each batch is 3.3x smaller, so the drain rate under throttle rises about 3x. That removes the queue cliff of idea 2 as a side effect, and the queued RSS drops 3-4x. Scaling idea 1's +3-8% for about 3.3 cores gives about +2-5%, and the feature stays on every node.
evidence: native_executor.rs:246-297 TradeKvs::build: trade_id = trade_index as u128 (16 B), height and timestamp repeated in all three values, user value duplicates the trade row (74 B)

metrics compaction_cpu_micros 317 s/node; flush_write_bytes 2.10 GB; compact_write_bytes 2.91 GB (write-amp so far about 1.4)
pending compaction bytes: CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES alone 148/346/285 MB, the largest CF on every node
bench_cmd --senders 5000; summary fills_per_native_block 58,579
ideas.expected_improvement: −60-70% trade-history rows and bytes; about 2 host cores freed; +2-5% matched/s, and the writer backlog cliff removed
ideas.risk: Node-local format change (RPC readers and tests; the frozen-encoder test in trade_kvs_tests.rs must be replaced). The aggregation gain depends on how many fills each address has per block. It is high in the bench and with market makers, but with many retail users it falls toward the key-only saving (bytes, not rows). No consensus risk.
ideas.why_new: Not in s64. The August matched-200k backlog listed a 'trade-kvs-arena-and-user-index-diet' by name only: the arena half landed (5582366 / e4cf9a4), and the index half was never specified or built. This proposal gives the concrete layout, moves row building to the writer thread, and bases the estimate on the new per-entry compaction cost and CPU attribution.

output.notes:
Answer to the angle's core question: trade history does NOT meaningfully block consensus directly. The hotstuff thread has no lock in common with the trade writer. RocksDB write grouping is rare: write_other/write_self delta is 973/56,032, about 1.7%, with pipelined write on. Trade chunks are 2048 rows (about 620 KB) and low_pri throttling happens before the write group is joined, so a consensus write waits at most about 1 ms behind a chunk. The costs are indirect: (a) host CPU, about 3 of 18 cores (writer + compaction + flush; the trade CFs are 84-100% of pending compaction bytes); (b) about 48% of WAL bytes, which also inflates restart WAL replay (this supports s64 item 3, the WAL cap); (c) RSS in the queue; (d) a latent exec stall once the 256-batch queue fills (idea 2).

Evidence that changes s64 estimates:
- s64's 'drop low_pri' for the trade writer would stop the throttle-driven backlog, but it would add about 0.2-0.3 cores per node of writer CPU and more trade compaction, all in direct competition with consensus threads. Pair it with idea 1 or 3 rather than doing it alone.
- The 'Renice rocksdb:low' item gets its CPU mostly from trade-CF compaction, so ideas 1 and 3 attack the same CPU at the source.
- The August 'history-db-split' (a separate history RocksDB instance with WAL off) is still a valid follow-on. It is not in s64 and was never built. Its incremental value over s64's WAL-off: the trade CFs' compaction debt and L0 would no longer count toward the shared instance's write controller (db.rs:280-283 notes that a slowdown on any CF throttles every writer), and the main WAL would halve. rust-rocksdb 0.24's Env is the shared default, so separate niced compaction pools would need a custom Env. I rate it +0-3% at 300 s, mainly robustness.

Smaller findings:
- The on_commit_block handler (main.rs:872-893) runs scan_trades_for_block on every commit, even with zero WS subscribers. When rows are present that is up to about 58.6k serde_json::Value objects with 7 format! calls each. It runs on the unnamed event-bus thread, which is unbounded and off the hotstuff thread. Measured unnamed-thread CPU is only about 4% of a core per node, so the throughput value is ≤0.5%. Gating it on `new_trades.receiver_count()>0` belongs with the s64 bug-6 fix.
- `torus_trade_writer_queued_batches` is only set on send (app.rs:2148-2150), so it freezes at its last value after load stops. Every metrics-after file reports a stale 50-102.
- flush_count reads 0 while flush bytes grow; s64 already notes this.
- The exec-thread cost of stamping and pushing trade rows in serial pass B is about 58.6k × ~150 ns ≈ 9 ms per block (pass B is 116 ms per native block). Idea 3 removes most of it, as does idea 1 fully.

All numbers come from the s65-votefix-fix-r1 and ctl-r2 cells, the s65-zerocode cells and s60-sustained-fixed-off-600-r1. Files read (read-only) include /home/18c/projects/wt/s63-body-fetch/crates/torus-state/src/bg_writer.rs, crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs, crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs, crates/torus-node/src/main.rs, crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs, crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs and crates/torus-state/src/db.rs.

ideas.title: Shrink trade-history writes: one user-index row per (trader, block), an append-only primary key, and a switch to turn history off on validators
ideas.area: torus-bridge TradeKvs / route_trade_kvs; torus-state bg_writer + CF_NATIVE_TRADES / CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES; torus-rpc get_user_trades / get_trades
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (0) Measure first. Add a node env TORUS_TRADE_HISTORY=0 that skips route_trade_kvs and the writer. Today trade_writer=None falls back to synchronous puts (app.rs:2138-2146), so no switch exists yet. A/B it at cap 200, n=3 per arm, to get the upper bound. It is also a legitimate production setting for validators that serve no RPC. (1) Stop writing two 106-byte CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES rows per fill (maker + taker, TradeKvs::build native_executor.rs:242-306). The trade writer thread instead builds one row per (trader, block): key trader(20)|desc_block(8); value a packed list of (market_id u64, trade_index u32, role u8), 13 B per entry. get_user_trades (torus-rpc torus.rs:1674) then prefix-scans those rows and multi_gets the primary CF_NATIVE_TRADES rows for price, qty and side. (2) Optionally re-key CF_NATIVE_TRADES as block(8)|market(8)|idx(4). New keys then always sort after all existing keys, so leveled compaction can trivially move files (write amplification about 1). The per-block scan at rpc lib.rs:481 becomes a single seek. Per-market recent-trade reads (torus.rs:941/1434) must then filter across blocks, or keep a small market|block pointer index. Both CFs are node-local and outside the native root (bg_writer.rs:1-10), so consensus is unaffected; the RPC format changes.
ideas.reasoning: The trade-history path is now about a quarter of each validator's CPU on a host with no idle CPU. Per node in the s65-votefix-fix-r1 load window (threads.log, 304 samples): torus-trade-writer 0.40 cores, rocksdb:low (compaction) 0.74, rocksdb:high (flush) 0.21, out of about 4.06 cores per node. compaction_cpu_micros is 315 s over the ~370 s cell (0.85 core). At the end of the cell only three CFs carry compaction debt: user_trades 148 MB, trades 113 MB, native_pending 51 MB. That puts 84% of the debt on the two trade CFs. RocksDB bytes_written is 14.33 GB per node per cell. Trade rows account for 22.44M fills × 297 B ≈ 6.7 GB (~47%), and the user index alone for 212 B/fill ≈ 4.76 GB (~33%). The user index has random trader-prefixed keys across 5000 senders, so every L0 file overlaps the whole key range: the worst case for write amplification. Only ~495 distinct traders are touched per block (dirty balance entries 189,605 / 383 blocks). Aggregating therefore turns ~117k user rows per block into ≤~500, and ~12.4 MB into ~1.5 MB per block (−88%). Estimated savings per node: trade-writer rows/bytes down ~65%, about −0.25 core. Compaction on the user CF is −88% of bytes, and the trades CF becomes trivial moves: −0.35 to −0.5 core. Flush: −0.05 to −0.1 core. Total ~0.65-0.85 core per node, ~2-2.5 cores host-wide (11-14% of 18 cores). The host is saturated in the load window: vmstat us+sy 95-98%, idle 2-4%, runqueue r = 29-83. The freed CPU goes to exec, hotstuff-algo and verify threads that are now runnable-waiting. By analogy with the renice estimate in s64 (+3-8%), I estimate +2-8% matched/s. Step 0 measures it directly. A side effect: the writer's low_pri throttle is triggered by compaction debt, and that debt is mostly self-inflicted by these two CFs.

ideas.title: Hand the fills, not the rows, to the trade writer: take trade-row build, index stamping and fill drops off exec settle pass A and pass B
ideas.area: torus-bridge native_executor.rs settle_market_results_parallel / compute_market_settle_plan / route_trade_kvs; torus-state bg_writer
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In compute_market_settle_plan (native_executor.rs:4446-4555), stop building Vec<TradeKvs> per order: 297 B per fill, about 17 MB per block. In pass B (4368-4375), replace the per-fill stamp_trade_index plus 3 PackedCfBatch pushes. For each successful order, pass B instead records (market_id, base_trade_index = ctx.trade_index, fills) and advances ctx.trade_index by fills.len(). The fills Vec is moved out of the owned MarketBatchResult results, which is O(1). In the common case with no failed orders this can be one entry per market, since failures already force the sequential fallback. Send a TradeJob {block_height, timestamp, entries} to the trade writer thread. That thread builds the byte-identical rows (or the aggregated rows from the history idea) and frees the fills there. Keep persist_trade for the sequential fallback path. Also pre-size the arena from the known fill count, which is useful even alone.
ideas.reasoning: Settle is the largest engine sub-phase on the exec critical chain. Pass B, the serial half, is 44.58 s / 383 = 116 ms per native block at 58.6k fills per block. The exec chain is 672 ms per block and runs exec-bound in the last ~120 s. The only per-pass-B attribution (s60, TORUS_SETTLE_PASSB_DIAG) put trade routing at 81-95 ms of 166-194 ms (49-50%). The packed-arena change then removed 6 small allocations per fill but was never benchmarked. What routing still does per block: ~176k pushes, stamping 58.6k TradeKvs, reading ~17 MB of rows that pass-A workers wrote on other cores (cache-cold), growing a fresh ~17 MB arena plus a ~7 MB row vector (mem::take leaves an empty PackedCfBatch every block, so page faults and zeroing recur), and cross-thread frees of each order's trades Vec and fills Vec. My estimate is 15-45 ms of routing plus 5-10 ms of drops that leave the serial path, and pass A loses its 17 MB of row writes. Arithmetic: −20 to −50 ms on a 672 ms chain is −3 to −7%. That is roughly +3-7% matched/s in the exec-bound late window, and with the ~0.4 weight of that window, +1-3% on the 300 s average. It also shrinks each queued writer batch from ~24 MB of rows to ~7.5 MB of fills (58.6k × ~128 B). The writer lags by up to 55 batches, so that is ~0.9 GB less RSS.

ideas.title: Collapse pass-B balance mutations to one read-modify-write per trader: aggregate PnL and margin releases in pass A
ideas.area: torus-bridge native_executor.rs settle pass A plan / pass B balance apply
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In compute_market_settle_plan, accumulate per trader within the market: pnl_sum, release_sum (taker margin_release plus the maker_releases amounts) and a touched flag. This replaces the per-order pnl_events Vec and maker_releases list. Emit them as a Vec sorted by address. In pass B, first merge the markets' aggregates per trader, then prefetch every touched balance through bal_cache.load. If any read fails, return to the sequential path before any mutation. Then apply, in sorted trader order: rel = min(release_sum, order_margin); order_margin -= rel; available += rel + pnl_sum; set(). This matches the old result exactly. Sequential clamped releases against one order_margin always release min(sum, order_margin) in total, pnl never touches order_margin, and FixedPoint addition is exact checked i128, so the order does not matter below overflow. Traders that only had Some(ZERO) events or zero releases are still set, so the row still exists as it does today.
ideas.reasoning: s60 attribution measured 16.04M balance attempts for 15.52M fills, about 1.03 per fill, which is ~60k per block now. Balance apply cost 28-32 ms per pass-B invocation. The in-place cache change (e4340d8) cut about 0.3 ms per 1k fills from pass B, so balance apply is now roughly 10-14 ms per block. Only ~495 distinct traders per block need a balance write (dirty_entries_balances 189,605/383). Aggregating turns ~60k map lookups and clones into ≤~500 plus a sort of the per-market lists. It also removes the ~tens of thousands of small pnl_events Vec allocations made in pass A and freed on the exec thread in pass B. Estimate: −12-18 ms on the serial exec chain (672 ms), i.e. −2 to −2.7%. That is +2-3% in the exec-bound late window and about +0.8-1.1% on the 300 s average. The saving is small but certain, and it also removes the ordering constraint that forces balance work to stay serial.

ideas.expected_improvement: pass B −12-18 ms per block; +0.8-1.1% matched/s on the 300 s average (+2-3% in the late window)
ideas.risk: Changes consensus-visible execution only in the overflow corner: a panic could fire at a different point with sums near i128 max, which is unreachable for realistic supply. It needs the byte-identical OFF/ON state-root test that parallel_settle_tests already uses. The error semantics for balance-read failures move to a prefetch-then-fallback design and need a targeted test.

The earlier options were balance-cache-inplace (faster per event, landed) and pass-B parallel shard-apply (s64/matched-200k backlog). This removes the per-fill balance events altogether, using a proven commutativity of the clamp.

output.notes:
New evidence and possible issues, all from s65-votefix-fix-r1 (f05b20e):
1. Latent exec backpressure cliff and RAM growth from the trade writer. torus_trade_writer_queued_batches (sampler.csv col 84, val0) climbs from 2-6 to 55 over the last ~180 s of load. The writer falls behind as compaction debt grows, and its low_pri writes are throttled by that debt (bg_writer.rs:27-29). Its queue is bounded at 256 (app.rs:3262). At the observed growth of ~0.35 batches/s, a load run longer than ~12-15 min would fill the queue and block the exec thread on send_packed. Each queued PackedCfBatch holds ~17 MB of rows plus ~7 MB of row descriptors, so the 55 batches hold ~1.3 GB. That accounts for part of the "RSS 124 MB → 7.7 GB" note in s64. The gauge is set only on send, so after load it reads a stale 55.
2. Trade history as a share of the node: rocksdb:low, trade-writer and rocksdb:high threads together average ~1.35 cores/node in the load window (of ~4.06), and about 1.0-1.1 of that is attributable to the trade CFs. Only gossip verification uses more.
3. A hypothesis for s64 item 9 (the HotStuff futex wait), not verified. The flush worker's state write is one atomic WriteBatch per block (~4.35 MB; state_write_db 161 ms/block = 61.67 s/383). The trade writer is chunked into 2048-row groups; the flush worker's batch is not. With TORUS_ROCKSDB_PIPELINED_WRITE=1, a small HotStuff-thread write (vote state, insert_persist) that lands behind this batch's memtable stage may wait tens of ms in RocksDB's WriteThread, which sleeps in futex. The flush worker is inside that write ~18% of wall time. Worth checking in the planned vote-state-write work (A) with RocksDB PerfContext write_thread_wait_nanos.
4. Production only: with TORUS_SYNC_WAL_ON_COMMIT=1, the per-commit flush_wal(true) (db.rs:487) also fsyncs ~17 MB/block of trade rows sharing the WAL. That strengthens the s64 disable_wal item for the trade CFs.
5. Considered and rejected as low value: a resident Position/Balance cache kept across blocks. Only ~2861 position reads and ~495 balance reads fall through per block (dirty_entries_positions 1,095,650/383 and balances 189,605/383), a few ms spread over the pass-A workers. Positions are ~82% of native-root dirty leaves per block (2861 of ~3480), so if root/trie work ever returns to the critical path, the position-row layout is where to look. That fits the existing s64 "trie internal nodes in RAM" item.
6. Exec breakdown per native block (val0): engine 449 ms (phase1 107, margin 29, match 105, settle 205 = pass A 80 + pass B 116 + cache flush 5), save_books 127, verify 42.5. Flush 393 ms is pipelined on the flush worker (root 110, state_write 183).

ideas.title: Give the trade-history CFs their own compaction profile: tiered (universal) compaction, LZ4 at the bottom level, no full-key bloom filter
ideas.area: torus-state db.rs open_with_tuning: per-CF options for CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES and CF_NATIVE_TRADES
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In StateDb::open_with_tuning (crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:276-332), build a `history_opts` clone for CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES and CF_NATIVE_TRADES, the same way `meta_opts` and `churny_opts` are built today. Settings: (a) set_bottommost_compression_type(Lz4) instead of Zstd. This is step 0: one line, and it cannot change behaviour. (b) set_compaction_style(Universal) with UniversalCompactOptions: size_ratio ~10, min_merge_width 4, max_size_amplification_percent 10000 (these CFs are append-only with unique keys, so there is no garbage to reclaim). Also raise this CF's level0_file_num_compaction_trigger to ~8 and slowdown/stop to 40/60, so the DB-wide write controller never throttles consensus writes because of history files. (c) Use a BlockBasedOptions with no bloom filter. Both CFs are only ever range-scanned (torus-rpc torus.rs:941/1434/1688, lib.rs:492; the get_cf callers are only in bg_writer tests). Optionally add a 20-byte prefix extractor with a prefix bloom on user_trades for the per-user RPC scans. Put all of it behind one env flag (TORUS_ROCKSDB_HISTORY_PROFILE=1) and A/B it n=3 in the s65 harness. Primary signals: torus_rocksdb_compaction_cpu_micros delta, rocksdb:low %CPU in threads.log, exec/hotstuff runqueue wait in schedstat.json, then matched/s. Node-local CFs outside every root, so there is no consensus or format risk. Existing SSTs can be reopened under universal.
ideas.reasoning: The LOG from a 3-minute devnet run (~/torus-wsl-devnet/data/val0/LOG, 2026-09-18, RocksDB 10.4.2, same shared options) attributes compaction CPU per CF: cf_native_user_trades 38.9 s and cf_native_trades 7.6 s, out of 54.2 s total. That is 86%. The cost is quadratic in elapsed time. The user key is addr(20)‖desc_block‖idx (native_executor.rs:284-294), so every flushed L0 file overlaps the whole key range. With dynamic level bytes, each L0→L6 compaction therefore rewrites the entire CF. The LOG jobs 16/29/46 read 4.05M → 8.1M → 12.2M records (4@0, then 4@0+1@6, then 4@0+2@6) for 6.3 → 13.2 → 17.5 CPU-s, with outputs of 41 → 82 → 122 MB, i.e. the whole CF each time. The s65 cell shows the same growth: in s65-votefix-fix-r1 val0, compaction CPU rose from 0.09 to 1.74 cores over the cell (sampler.csv, 30 s steps), and the total was 317 CPU-s per node in ~370 s. threads.log puts rocksdb:low at 77% of a core per node. Per node, at 86% share, trade compaction ≈ 273 CPU-s per cell. Leveled with full overlap reads about D·(k+1)/2 for k compactions. At ~8 compactions per cell that is ~4.5x the data. Tiered with fanout 4-10 gives about log(D/F) ≈ 1.5-2.5x. That saves ~45-65%, and LZ4 instead of zstd saves another ~20%. Zstd costs ~5 ns/byte here: pending job 35 compressed 772 MB raw in 3.8 CPU-s, and user_trades bottom output is ~2.2 GB raw per 3 min, so ≈11 of its 38.9 s. Combined: ~55-75% of 273 s ≈ 150-205 CPU-s per node, or 0.4-0.55 core/node on average and ~1-1.3 core/node in the exec-bound last 2 minutes. Across three nodes that frees ~1.2-1.7 cores on average and ~3-4 late, on a host where load is 30-33 on 18 CPUs. The host is CPU-oversubscribed. schedstat shows the exec thread waiting 40-46 s in the runqueue and hotstuff-algo 33-35 s over the 305 s window. pidstat shows exec at 31% run and 30% runqueue-wait. Removing ~5% of runnable demand on average and ~10-12% late cuts those waits proportionally: about 5 ms per committed block on hotstuff, and ~3-5% more exec throughput in the late window. That gives roughly +0.5-3% matched/s on a 300 s cell. The larger effect is on long runs. Leveled compaction CPU grows linearly with elapsed time (the per-cell trend extrapolates to ~5 cores/node by ~20 minutes), and this change removes that growth.

ideas.title: Store native-action bodies as RocksDB blob files (BlobDB) in CF_NATIVE_PENDING and CF_BLOCK_BODIES
ideas.area: torus-state db.rs per-CF options for the DA / body CFs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Add a `body_opts` clone for CF_NATIVE_PENDING, CF_BLOCK_BODIES and CF_COMMIT_MANIFEST (optional) with: set_enable_blob_files(true), set_min_blob_size(2048), set_blob_compression_type(Lz4), set_enable_blob_garbage_collection(false) (nothing is deleted today; see s64 bug 8), and set_blob_file_size ~256 MiB. Share the existing 256 MiB cache as the blob cache, or leave it unset: blob reads are one pread served from the page cache. Keep the bloom filter on CF_NATIVE_PENDING, because presence checks by action hash use it. Env-gate the change and A/B it together with idea 1 or on its own. Measure compaction_cpu_micros, torus_view_insert_persist_seconds and body-serve latency on the hotstuff thread.
ideas.reasoning: Bodies are large and highly compressible: cf_native_pending averages 19.5 KB per KV at 9.77x raw/compressed, and cf_block_bodies ~500 KB per KV at 8.93x. Under leveled compaction with zstd at the bottom level, every L0→L6 compaction decompresses and re-compresses all bodies accumulated so far. The CF never shrinks, because NativeDaStore::remove has no production caller (s64 bug 8), so its compaction cost is quadratic like the trade CFs. In the 3-minute LOG, pending job 35 spent 3.8 CPU-s on 39,575 records (~772 MB raw), about 5 ns/byte, which is mostly zstd. Pending plus bodies were 6.5 s of 54.2 s of compaction CPU (12%). Scaled to the s65 cell (317 CPU-s per node), that is ~38 CPU-s per node. With blob files the value is written once at flush (LZ4, ~1 ns/byte), and compaction afterwards moves only ~40-byte keys and blob indexes. That removes ~90% of that cost (~34 CPU-s per node per cell ≈ 0.09 core/node, ~0.3 core host-wide) and keeps it flat as the CF grows. The throughput effect in a 300 s cell is small (+0-1%). The main value is that a body CF which grows without bound stops making compaction CPU grow with the square of run time. It also stops hundreds of MB of 10x-compressible bodies from being re-compressed by zstd on the same cores that exec and hotstuff wait for.

Every body read becomes an extra pread (from page cache). The hotstuff thread serves body fetches (s64 §3), so time that serve path. Without GC, blob files never shrink, which is no worse than today's never-pruned CF.

It says nothing about how RocksDB stores and compacts them. Blob files, and the 5 ns/byte zstd re-compression cost measured in the LOG, are not in s64 or the planned A/B/C items.

output.notes:
I found three new RocksDB-option ideas. None of them speeds up consensus directly, and storage CPU is a real cost on this host; the evidence for each is in the ideas above.

1. **Much of the angle is already in the code.** Bloom filters (10 bits/key), a 256 MiB shared LRU block cache, 16 KiB blocks, pinned L0 index and filter blocks, LZ4 with Zstd at the bottom level, dynamic level bytes, an 8 MiB memtable for consensus_meta and a 1 GiB global memtable cap all landed in 7cdd22b and later (db.rs:257-291). I did not re-propose them.

2. **The 44 column families cost little in themselves.** Only about 7 CFs receive meaningful writes. Merging CFs would not help. The WAL cost of the CF count is s64 item 3.

3. **The WAL is dominated by highly compressible data.** WAL bytes were 14.33 GB per node per cell, about 34 MB per native block, and identical across validators. Flush output was only 2.1 GB. Bodies and trade rows compress 9-10x with LZ4.
   - WAL compression (`set_wal_compression_type(Zstd)`) would cut that volume a lot, but it adds zstd work (~5 ns/byte) to the serialized write path. That makes it a net loss on this CPU-bound host, so I did not propose it.

4. **Two stated premises look wrong.**
   - `write_other` was 974 against about 56k own writes in the window. That is about 1.7%, so RocksDB write-group queuing is rare. It is a weak argument that storage causes the hotstuff futex wait, which fits "storage is not the blocker".
   - The host is CPU-oversubscribed. Load average was 30-33 on 18 CPUs. pidstat shows ingress-verify at 249% waiting to run, rpc-worker at 167% and exec at 30%. schedstat shows hotstuff-algo waiting to run for 33-35 s of the 305 s window in every arm.
   - At RATE=270 the waits did not drop (hotstuff 33-34 s), yet blocks/s rose to 1.19-1.41. So the ~8% gain at 270 does not come from freeing CPU. Anyone who assumes freed CPU turns straight into throughput should discount it. My % estimates for ideas 1-2 are kept low for this reason.

5. **The trade writer is falling behind.** Its queue grew from 4 to 55 batches over the cell (`torus_trade_writer_queued_batches`), while its thread used 42% CPU and waited 18% for CPU. That fits s64's "low_pri limiter pins it" and is not new.

6. **The state flush write looks slow.** `exec_state_write_db` takes about 150-200 ms per block for a ~4.3 MB batch. That is about 4 µs per row, and it runs on torus-flush-worker (28.7% CPU). It is not a RocksDB-option problem that I could attribute. Once the LOG is kept (idea 3), check whether that time is memtable insert CPU or waiting.

7. **The LOG evidence is from another commit.** It comes from a leftover September 18 devnet (~/torus-wsl-devnet/data/val0, 3-minute run). The s65 cell's own numbers (compaction CPU rising from 0.09 to 1.74 cores, 317 CPU-s total) behave the same quadratic way.

8. **Idea 1 has a zero-risk first step.** Setting LZ4 at the bottom level of the trade CFs, instead of Zstd, is worth ~20% of their compaction CPU. It can be A/B'd on its own.

ideas.title: Exec thread: stop re-encoding, re-hashing and deep-cloning every block body just to sort it (sort_native_actions / replay-guard clone)
ideas.area: torus-bridge native_executor.rs sort_native_actions / sort_deterministic; torus-consensus app.rs execute_committed_block_with (replay guard + sort call)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Keep the result exactly the same and remove the waste around it. (1) Replace `sort_native_actions(&[(Address, NativeAction)])`, which does `action.clone()` for every action (native_executor.rs:6033) and then `keccak256(action.canonical_bytes())` per action as the tiebreak key (:6051-6054), with a version that takes the Vec by value. It should compute the keys (category, sender, keccak(canonical_bytes)) into a Vec<(key, idx)>, sort the indices, and move the actions out, with no second clone. (2) Compute the 200 keys in parallel on scoped threads, chunked the way match_parallel/phase2_parallel_prepare already are. Reuse one encode buffer per worker, sized up front, instead of `Vec::with_capacity(64)` growing about 10 times per 18 KB action (torus-types lib.rs:675-676). (3) Optionally drop the replay-guard deep clone (`sender_actions.push((sender, signed.action.clone()))`, app.rs:1750): execute_batch_inner already flattens by reference (C2), so an `execute_batch` variant over `&[(Address, &NativeAction)]` removes the last copy of about 80k PlaceOrderParams. (4) Put an `exec_sort_seconds` timer around the call at app.rs:1781, since that window is untimed today. Variant with a consensus change (lockstep deploy only): break ties by block position, or by the action hashes that dispatch_to_exec already computes (app.rs ~5446), passed through CommittedBlockMsg. That removes the hashing entirely but changes the execution order of same-sender batches.
ideas.reasoning: Cost per native block at cap 200 with 400-order batches: canonical encoding is 45 B per order (8+1+16+16+1+1+1+1, FixedPoint is an i128), so 400×45 ≈ 18 KB per action and ≈3.6 MB per block. keccak at the 248 MB/s used in s64 takes ≈14.5 ms. The encode is ≈5-8 ms: the analogous bincode body encode measures 8.2 ms per native block (commit_body_encode 3.16 s / 383). Two deep clones of ≈80k PlaceOrderParams (~128 B each, ≈10 MB per clone) take ≈3-5 ms each. Total ≈23-30 ms per native block on the single exec thread. Upper bound check: the exec thread's untimed residual (exec_block − verify − replay_guard − load_books − engine − save_books − handoff − body_persist − evm) is 38-45 ms per native block on all 6 node-cells of s65-votefix-fix-r1 and ctl-r2 (≈674 ms per native block total), so the estimate fits inside what is unattributed. The parallel exact variant leaves ~3 ms, so it saves ≈20-27 ms, or −3-4% of exec wall per native block. Throughput only moves in the exec-bound late window (~last 120 s of 300 s, per s64). +3-4% there × 0.4 ≈ +1.2-1.6% on matched_s_avg, plus a little headroom that item 1 of s64 will need once consensus speeds up. That is below the 9-10% MDE, so validate on exec_block_seconds per native block and the new timer, not on matched/s.

NEW EVIDENCE for s64 item 4 ("seed the follower OnceLock"): the cold PendingProposal OnceLock is hit on the leader's produce path too, not only at commit. select_block_payload (app.rs:5076-5080) calls native_action_hashes() on every pending_proposals entry. The parent block (H-1) was validated as a follower via finish_validate → PendingProposal::new (OnceLock empty, app.rs:4566, 700) and is not committed yet at produce time, so a full 200-action canonical+keccak pass (~4 MB, ≈15-20 ms) runs inside block_build_seconds (build_timer starts before selection, app.rs:4634). Seeding the OnceLock from the CompactBlock hashes at reconstruct time (which is just as trusted as the DA store) would take ≈15-20 ms off the ~185 ms leader block_build as well as off commit. That raises item 4's value by roughly +1-3%.

OTHER OBSERVATIONS
- TORUS_EXEC_PIPELINE is now default ON (exec_pipeline.rs:45). Every 100th block (epoch boundary) takes the serial barrier path; h700 took 1.13 s against the ~674 ms mean. This costs ~0.7% of exec time, so it is not worth doing.

ideas.title: View deadlines are anchored to the epoch-entry Instant, not the view-entry Instant: sustained views >500 ms make every QC-entered view arrive with an already-expired deadline
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs pacemaker (timers)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In crates/hotstuff_rs/src/pacemaker/implementation.rs `update_view` step 3 (lines 636-648), never enter a view with less than one slot remaining: `deadline = max(scheduled, Instant::now() + max_view_time * multiplier)` (mirror of the existing 2c stretch at :625-633, but applied for multiplier == 1 too), or equivalently rebase the schedule when `scheduled < now` the same way 2b (:610) rebases when it is >2 slots in the future. Keep the epoch schedule for the ahead-of-schedule clamp. Add a gauge `view_deadline_slack_ms = scheduled - now` recorded at every update_view so the mechanism can be confirmed in one cell before/after. Add a unit test next to `update_view_jump_rebases_stale_schedule` (:1468) asserting a view entered 2 s behind schedule still gets a full max_view_time.
ideas.reasoning: The per-epoch schedule assigns deadline(v) = epoch_start_instant + max_view_time * (v - base + 1) (initial_timeouts :830-841, update_timeouts :885-900; genesis: epoch_length 100, timeout_base_ms 500 -> devnet/genesis.json). `update_view` looks the scheduled Instant up and adopts it unchanged when the stall multiplier is 1 (:636-648); the only rebase (2b, :610) fires when the schedule is >2 slots in the FUTURE; the code comment at :582-589 explicitly says a replica that is behind schedule "burns through" views. `tick` publishes ViewTimeout as soon as `Instant::now() > deadline` (:103) and then broadcasts a TimeoutVote AND locally advances to cur+1 (:155-180). Measured load-window view time is ~620-660 ms against a 500 ms slot, so slack shrinks by 120-160 ms per view; after ~500/150 ≈ 3-4 views past each rebase (epoch entry every 100 views ≈ 60-70 s) every view entered via a QC has deadline < now on entry and is abandoned on the first tick, dropping the in-flight leader proposal for that view (n=3 needs all votes). That is a candidate mechanism for the measured ~1.5 views per committed block and 139 timeouts / (1.5 × 877) ≈ 10.5% of load-window views (s65-votefix-fix-r3 summary.json). Honest caveat: the naive model predicts more than 10.5% timeouts once behind, so some path (epoch rebase, TC-driven 2c stretch to now+1 s) is limiting it; the proposed gauge settles that. Ceiling if all 139 timeouts vanished: 1315/(1315-139) - 1 ≈ +12% blocks/s; block building stays the critical path, so +3-8% matched/s is realistic.

ideas.title: Session-key expiry is never enforced at execution: block timestamp (seconds) is compared against expiry (milliseconds)
ideas.area: torus-types eip712 / torus-consensus validate_block / torus-bridge validator
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Pass block time in milliseconds wherever a header timestamp meets session data: crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1649 (`batch_verify_native_actions_cached(&actions, torus_block.header.timestamp, ...)` -> `.saturating_mul(1000)`), crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:370 (`resolve_sender(block.header.timestamp, ...)`), and app.rs:1826/1839 if NativeExecContext::timestamp is ever used for ms comparisons elsewhere. Better: one `block_time_ms(header)` helper in torus-types used by exec_create_session (native_executor.rs:5416) and these two sites so the unit lives in one place. Add a test: create a session with expiry = now_ms + 1, validate a block whose header.timestamp is 1 s later carrying a session-signed action -> the action must be dropped (FIX 2 path) at app.rs:1722-1731.
ideas.reasoning: produce_block stamps `header.timestamp = SystemTime::now()...as_secs()` (app.rs:4633-4636), ≈1.79e9. Session expiry is milliseconds: MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS (eip712.rs:735-736) and exec_create_session converts explicitly (`now_ms = ctx.timestamp.saturating_mul(1000)`, native_executor.rs:5410-5420, with a comment stating the block timestamp is SECONDS), so any stored expiry is ≥ created_at_ms ≈ 1.79e12. batch_verify_impl then evaluates `timestamp <= session.expiry` (eip712.rs:1143) as 1.79e9 <= 1.79e12: always true; the catch-up validator path evaluates `current_timestamp > session.expiry` (eip712.rs:826 via validator.rs:370): always false. Result: an expired (or leaked-and-expired) session key remains valid forever at execution on every validator; the only enforcement is ingress with the local wall clock (torus.rs:486-489 -> validate_with_sessions in ms). Concrete failure: a market-maker's 24 h session key expires; a leader whose ingress admitted the action moments before expiry, or any Byzantine/patched leader holding session-signed intents, includes them a day later and all honest validators execute them. Same units bug would also make any future 'expired-session slash' misfire.

ideas.title: The 60 s nonce window is ingress-only: never-included signed intents stay executable forever, and header.timestamp is entirely unchecked
ideas.area: torus-consensus validate_block / torus-types eip712 / torus-bridge validator
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (1) In validate_block's FIX-2 drop pass (app.rs:1722-1731) and validator.rs:369-390, drop actions whose `nonce` is outside `header.timestamp*1000 ± (NONCE_WINDOW_MS + PIPELINE_SLACK_MS)` (slack ~120 s to cover the measured 35% mempool expiry tail and the 3-chain pipeline). Deterministic because it is evaluated against the header, not the local clock. (2) Add the missing header sanity check in validate_block: `header.timestamp >= parent.timestamp` and `header.timestamp <= local_now_secs + 5`; today no comparison of header.timestamp exists in app.rs or validator.rs. (3) Tests: block carrying an action whose nonce is 10 min older than header.timestamp must drop it; block with timestamp 1 h ahead of local clock must be rejected.
ideas.reasoning: eip712.rs:852-858 checks the ±60 s window only inside `validate()`/`validate_with_sessions()`, which are called from ingress (torus.rs:486-489; mempool lib.rs:428-436, 450-460, 570-580) with each node's own SystemTime. batch_verify_impl (eip712.rs:1095-1160) has no window check, and the exec replay guard (app.rs:1712-1750) only rejects (sender, nonce) pairs already consumed in CF_NATIVE_NONCES. Under the measured load ~35% of offered actions expire unincluded ≈ 0.35 × 343/s ≈ 120 signed intents per second whose nonces are never consumed; their bodies are durably mirrored on admission (`mirror_to_da`, lib.rs:437). Any leader that retains such a body (Byzantine, or a future bug that re-proposes DA-store bodies) can include it minutes or hours later and every honest validator executes it: a stale limit/market order at a price the user abandoned, or a stale cancel-all. Because nothing bounds header.timestamp, adding the exec-time window alone would let a skewed leader either bypass it (timestamp forward) or invalidate its own blocks silently (timestamp back); the header bound turns a skewed leader into a visible view timeout instead.

ideas.title: Validator wall-clock skew silently empties that validator's proposals (no skew detection anywhere)
ideas.area: torus-mempool ingest / torus-node telemetry (clock skew)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (1) Export a gauge `torus_proposal_clock_offset_seconds = local_now_secs - header.timestamp` recorded in the proposal-receive path (main.rs on_receive_proposal_header ~:862) and warn when |offset| > 10 s. (2) In the mempool ingest rejection paths (lib.rs:428-436, 450-460, 570-580) count `nonce too old` / `too future` separately per source; when one side dominates for >30 s, log a clock-skew warning naming the likely cause. (3) Optionally cross-check at startup: compare local clock with the latest committed header timestamp and refuse to become leader while |offset| > NONCE_WINDOW_MS/2. No consensus change.
ideas.reasoning: Every native-action admission path validates the ±60 s nonce window against the receiving node's own SystemTime, and eviction uses the same clock (native_pool.rs:456 `now_ms - NONCE_WINDOW_MS`). Consensus itself never compares clocks (no skew metric in torus-telemetry; no header.timestamp check). Failure scenario: validator V's clock is +70 s (VM restored from snapshot, NTP not yet stepped, or stepped after the node started). V still votes and leads normally, but every gossiped/forwarded action fails `nonce.saturating_add(60_000) < current_time_ms` at lib.rs:575, so V's native pool is empty and every block V leads is empty: at n=3 that is one third of leader slots -> up to -33% matched/s with no alarm, and if V is the RPC ingress node, 100% of client submissions are rejected. Partial skew s < 60 s shortens V's effective TTL to 60 - s s: with the pool sitting at ~60 s × 343/s ≈ 20k actions in the measured 35%-expiry regime, V's pool holds (60-s)/60 of what peers hold and its eviction order diverges, so which actions get included depends on which validator leads. Single-host devnet cannot exhibit this, which is why it has never shown up in cells.

ideas.title: Oracle aggregation, liquidation sweep and funding never run: the perp risk loop is unwired
ideas.area: torus-consensus/app.rs exec tail, torus-bridge/native_executor.rs, torus-node
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Wire `NativeExecutor::aggregate_oracle_prices` (native_executor.rs:5714) and `run_liquidation_checks` (:5733) into the post-engine tail in app.rs (after the two `execute_batch` calls at 1864-1865, next to `drain_core_writer` at 1889), behind a governance/genesis flag so devnet stays unchanged. 2) Add a validator-side price feeder in torus-node that signs `NativeAction::SubmitOraclePrices` (torus-types lib.rs:592) each N blocks — today no crate outside the executor/RPC references the oracle (crates/torus-node/src has zero oracle/funding hits; devnet/, docs/, tools/ have no feeder). 3) Implement funding: a per-market cumulative funding index updated in the tail from (mark - index), plus a per-position index snapshot; `Position` (position.rs:52-61) currently has no funding field and the only funding artifact in the tree is the `max_funding_rate_bps` parameter (torus-types lib.rs:1110). 4) Make `torus_get_mark_price` return an error or the last-trade price instead of mark=index=0 when no aggregated price exists (torus.rs:1638-1641).
ideas.reasoning: Grep over crates/ finds no caller of `aggregate_oracle_prices` or `run_liquidation_checks`; the only per-block tail work is `drain_core_writer`, `process_governance`, `distribute_fees`, `process_epoch_boundary` (app.rs:1889-1892). So the answer to 'do oracle/mark/funding updates run on the critical path' is: they run nowhere. Cost today is literally the tail histogram: s65-votefix-fix-r1 val1 `torus_exec_post_engine_tail_seconds_sum` = 0.0748 s over 383 blocks = 0.195 ms/block versus `torus_exec_engine_seconds_sum` 174.84 s / 383 = 456 ms/block, i.e. 0.04% of the engine window. Failure scenario: fills open positions via `positions.apply_fill` (native_executor.rs:4885-4910) with entry price = fill price; as the book price moves, no block ever computes a mark price, so an account whose losses exceed its collateral is never liquidated, no ADL/insurance path runs, and no funding pulls the perp toward index. `torus_get_positions` silently prices unrealized PnL at entry (torus.rs:790-794) and `torus_get_mark_price` reports 0 (torus.rs:1638-1641), so operators cannot see the drift.

ideas.title: OracleManager::collect_submissions is an unbounded full-prefix scan with a 100-key prune cap
ideas.area: torus-core/oracle.rs, torus-state overlay iterate_cf
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Re-key submissions as (market_id, block_number BE, validator) so `aggregate_price` does a bounded range scan over [window_start, current_block] and prunes with a range delete below window_start; or simpler, key by (market_id, validator) and overwrite on each `submit_price` so at most V entries exist per market and no pruning is needed. Drop the `prune_limit = 100` loop (oracle.rs:325-328). Also make `submit_price` reject block_number/price submissions older than the window so the CF cannot be grown by stale entries.
ideas.reasoning: `collect_submissions` (oracle.rs:299-333) calls `iterate_cf(CF_NATIVE_ORACLE, prefix=market)` which returns ALL submissions ever stored for that market, borsh-decodes each one, and deletes at most 100 stale keys per call. On the exec overlay, `iterate_cf` (backend.rs:1114-1136) does a RocksDB prefix scan, collects into a BTreeMap, merges parent + pending layers under the pending RwLock, then re-collects into a Vec — allocation proportional to the full history. Growth arithmetic: V validators x M markets new keys per block. Devnet-like 3 x 1 x 1.1 blocks/s x 86,400 s = 285k keys/day with aggregation unwired (nothing ever prunes). Once wired, with 100 validators x 50 markets = 5,000 keys/block versus prune of 100/block per market call (50 calls x 100 = 5,000/block) the backlog only breaks even; any missed block or higher V grows it forever. Cost when it is large: 100 validators x 86,400 blocks = 8.6M decodes per market per aggregate, seconds per block, all inside the exec tail that is currently 0.2 ms.

crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:138-160 submission_key = market||validator||block
crates/torus-state/src/backend.rs:1114-1136 overlay iterate_cf merges into BTreeMap under pending read lock
crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5522-5529 submit_price per (market,price) with no pruning
ideas.expected_improvement: O(V) instead of O(history) per market per block once aggregation is wired; removes unbounded CF_NATIVE_ORACLE growth (285k keys/day on the devnet shape)
ideas.risk: Key-format change to a state CF: needs a migration or genesis-only rollout; state-root affected if CF_NATIVE_ORACLE is in the native trie.
ideas.why_new: No perf doc or memory entry discusses oracle CF growth or the prune cap; the s64 list has no oracle entries.

ideas.title: Liquidation sweep as written costs 3 state prefix scans per trader per market per block
ideas.area: torus-bridge/native_executor.rs run_liquidation_checks, torus-core/liquidation.rs, margin.rs, position.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Before wiring the sweep (finding 1), replace the scan-everything design: keep a per-market in-memory position index next to the resident order books (trader -> size/entry/margin, rebuilt at boot like ResidentBooks), maintained from `apply_fill`; keep per-market BTreeMaps of open positions keyed by estimated liquidation price (longs ascending, shorts descending) and on each new mark price only visit the entries the price crossed. Run the sweep once per block over all markets, not per market over all traders, and pass the position slice into `check_cross_liquidation` so `cross_margin_equity` / `total_maintenance_margin` do not re-scan.
ideas.reasoning: `run_liquidation_checks` (native_executor.rs:5733-5754) loops over every market config and calls `check_liquidations(traders)`; that loops every trader (liquidation.rs:80-109) and calls `positions_for_trader` (position.rs:260-271, one `iterate_cf` prefix scan); for cross accounts `check_cross_liquidation` then calls `cross_margin_equity` (margin.rs:184-185: get_native_balance + positions_for_trader again) and `total_maintenance_margin` (margin.rs:208: positions_for_trader a third time). Each overlay `iterate_cf` is a RocksDB prefix seek + BTreeMap merge + RwLock read (backend.rs:1114-1136). Arithmetic: M=10 markets, T=10k traders -> 10 x 10k x 3 = 300k prefix scans per block; at ~10 us each that is 3 s per block, 6.6x the measured 456 ms engine window (174.84 s / 383 blocks). Even M=1, T=1k: 3k scans ~ 30 ms = 6.6% of the engine window added to a tail that is 0.2 ms today. The exec thread is pipelined behind consensus (CTE) so this would not directly slow voting, but the engine window is already 456 ms against a ~640 ms view, so any tens-of-ms addition eats the remaining slack and backs up the exec pipeline.

ideas.risk: The in-memory index must be rebuilt deterministically on restart and kept consistent with CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS; liquidation-price ordering must be recomputed when leverage tiers or margin configs change.
ideas.why_new: Not in s64 or prior perf docs; the parallel round's 'risk/margin' angle covers per-order margin math, not the block-level sweep algorithm which has never executed.

ideas.title: Stop-order triggering rescans every pending stop on each fill-bearing order
ideas.area: torus-core/order_book.rs trigger_stops
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Store pending stops in two price-ordered BTreeMaps (buy stops keyed by trigger ascending, sell stops by trigger descending, values id-ordered) and in `trigger_stops` pop only the prefix crossed by `last_trade_price`; keep the id-ascending Vec order only at serialization time (order_book.rs:1377-1380 asserts it for rebuild). Alternatively trigger once per block after the batch via the existing but uncalled `check_stops` hook (order_book.rs:779-781; no callers in torus-bridge or torus-consensus) instead of after every fill.
ideas.reasoning: `place_order` calls `trigger_stops()` whenever a placement produced fills (order_book.rs:577-579). `trigger_stops` (1272-1330) runs `pending_stops.retain(...)` over the whole Vec, up to 10 rounds, cloning each fired stop. Cost is O(P) per fill-bearing placement. Arithmetic on the measured cell: ~60-65k fills/s at ~1.1 blocks/s is ~55k fills per block; if ~20k placements per block carry fills and P = 1,000 resting stops that is 20M predicate evaluations plus Vec compaction per block, ~40-60 ms at 2-3 ns each = 9-13% of the 456 ms engine window; at P = 10k it exceeds the entire window. The bench never places stops (P = 0), so this is invisible in every s65 cell and only appears when real users rest stops.

ideas.title: Make the commit manifest the durable body record; stop writing the 4.7 MB full body per block per validator
ideas.area: torus-consensus app.rs persist_committed_block_durably / torus-state block_body.rs / pruner.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) In `persist_committed_block_durably_timed` (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:864-935) stop calling `encode_body_record` and stop putting the ~4.7 MB record into CF_BLOCK_BODIES; keep the header put and KEEP the CF_COMMIT_MANIFEST row (today it is deleted in the same batch at app.rs:915-919). Also fold the standalone `persist_commit_manifest` put_cf_raw (app.rs:986) into that batch so the commit does one RocksDB write instead of two. 2) Add a reference record format in crates/torus-state/src/block_body.rs: tag 0x02 + the compact datum (or just the 200 x 32-byte hash list), and make `decode_body_record` resolve it through `NativeDaStore::get_batch` (native_da.rs:160) exactly as `reconstruct_compact_from_da` (app.rs:3690) already does. The only readers are `load_replay_body` (app.rs:1133, crash replay) and RPC `get_block_body` (crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1348); neither is on the hot path, and `exec_source_for_height` (app.rs:1037-1050) already turns a compact manifest into `ExecSource::Pull`. 3) Tie CF_NATIVE_PENDING retention to body retention: when `prune_range` (pruner.rs:206) drops heights, read each pruned reference record and delete its hashes from CF_NATIVE_PENDING (this also gives `NativeDaStore::remove` its missing production caller for committed actions). Gate behind an env flag; A/B on `torus_commit_persist_write_seconds`, `torus_commit_body_encode_seconds`, block_build and view length.
ideas.reasoning: Sizes: one PlaceOrderParams bincode = market_id 8 + is_buy 1 + price i128 16 + quantity i128 16 + order_type tag 4 + tif tag 4 + reduce_only 1 + Option<u64> 9 = 59 B; a 400-order PlaceOrderBatch = 4 + 8 + 400*59 + nonce 8 + sig (4+1+32+32) = 23,689 B; 200 actions = 4.74 MB per full block. The compact datum (header ~548 B + 8 + 200*32 hashes + 16) is ~6.97 KB, i.e. ~680x smaller. Every validator's `on_committed_block` writes the 4.74 MB record on the hotstuff thread even though the same bytes are already durable per action in CF_NATIVE_PENDING (ingress mirror + S459 proposer mirror + follower `absorb_fetched_bodies` app.rs:3919), and that CF is never pruned (s64 #8), so the references are always resolvable. Measured (s65-zerocode-r270-r1 val0, metrics-after-val0.txt): commit_persist_write 1234 of 1750 commits < 1 ms (small header/manifest batches), the other 516 sum to ~19.2 s = 37 ms mean, buckets 16-32 ms (117), 32-64 (74), 64-128 (52), 128-256 (19), >256 ms (7); commit_body_encode for those blocks ~2.37 s / ~350 full = 6.8 ms mean (147 in 4-8 ms, 70 in 8-16). So the size of the value, not write-group contention, is what puts ms-scale waits on the consensus thread (small batches under the same load stay < 0.5 ms). Removing encode + the big put saves ~35-45 ms per full block on each validator's consensus thread; with the next leader committing synchronously before it can propose (s64 item 1), that is 35-45 ms of a ~640 ms view = 5-7% of view time; assuming partial overlap, +3-6% matched/s standalone, +1-3% once in-progress item (C) moves the leader's commit feed off the pre-broadcast path (the thread is still occupied by the feed). Side effect: CF_BLOCK_BODIES ingest drops from ~5.2 MB/s per node (4.74 MB x 1.1 blocks/s, ~1.6 GB per 300 s cell, ~12 memtable flushes + L0->L1 LZ4 compactions) to ~8 KB/s.

ideas.title: State pruner cuts off by COMMITTED height, so bodies of committed-but-unexecuted heights can be pruned and crash replay fail-stops on a Hole
ideas.area: torus-node main.rs pruner wiring / torus-state pruner.rs / torus-consensus replay_gap
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Feed the pruner the applied (executed) height, or `min(committed, applied)`: in crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:1040 `pruner.maybe_prune(current)` reads `latest_height_shared`, which the commit handler stores at main.rs:880 from the hotstuff commit event. Either store the exec-side applied marker into a second AtomicU64 for the pruner, or clamp the cutoff in `StatePruner::maybe_prune` (pruner.rs:63-69) to the applied height. Add a unit test: committed=5000, applied=3500, retention=1000 must not prune bodies above 3500.
ideas.reasoning: Chain is CTE: execution lags commit under load (tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:2741-2744 notes eth_blockNumber lags consensus and drains after load). `maybe_prune` computes `cutoff = current_height - retention_blocks` (pruner.rs:69) and `prune_range` range-deletes CF_BLOCK_BODIES (pruner.rs:211-215). If exec lag ever exceeds `retention_blocks` (bench uses 100000 so never in cells; a production node with e.g. 1000 at ~1.1 blocks/s only needs ~15 min of backlog, or a long GC/stall on the exec thread), the body for a committed, non-empty, not-yet-executed height is deleted while the manifest was already dropped in the durable batch (app.rs:915-919, because the body WAS durable at the time). Live execution is unaffected (the TorusBlock is in the exec channel), but a crash in that window makes `replay_gap` (app.rs:1189+) hit `load_replay_body == None` on a header with native_action_count > 0 -> `ReplayGapOutcome::Hole` -> deliberate fail-stop, and the heal channel cannot recover it because the manifest is gone. Same coupling: CF_RECEIPTS for those heights and the RPC `pruned_up_to` gate would mark still-to-be-executed heights as pruned.

ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In crates/torus-state/src/block_body.rs `encode_ref` (BinV1 arm, ~lines 83-92) drop the `bincode::serialized_size` pre-pass. ideas.reasoning: `serialized_size` is a full serde traversal of 200 actions x 400 orders x 8 fields = 640k field visits through the SizeChecker; `serialize_into` then does the same traversal with copies. A size-only pass is typically 25-40% of the serialize cost, so ~1.5-2.5 ms per full block; 2 ms / 640 ms view = 0.3% of view time. Also the exec-side fallback (`TORUS_EXEC_REWRITE_DURABLE_ROWS=1`, app.rs:2169-2172) pays it again.

ideas.title: Native-action batches are delivered twice to every follower: flood-publish plus mesh cross-forward, each copy fully ed25519-verified before dedup
ideas.area: torus-network gossipsub (native-action topic)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:gossipsub_config add `.validate_messages()`; in the Gossipsub `Message` arm of handle_event (crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:1255-1420) call `gossipsub.report_message_validation_result(&message_id, &propagation_source, ..)` on every exit path: `Accept` for CONSENSUS_TOPIC/TX_TOPIC and for the native topic when the validator set is NOT fully connected, `Ignore` (deliver locally, never forward) for native-topic batches when every validator VK in the current set resolves in peer_map (helper `is_validator_peer` already exists at swarm.rs:685). Alternative with the same effect: move the native pre-spread onto the existing direct request/response fan (the B2 `consensus_direct_fan` machinery) and stop subscribing validators to the native topic. Also register gossipsub's own metrics (`Behaviour::new_with_metrics`) so duplicate receptions become visible; today no torus counter sees them.
ideas.reasoning: Topology: 3 validators, gossipsub defaults (libp2p-gossipsub 0.49.4 config.rs defaults: flood_publish=true, mesh_n_low=4 so every peer is grafted into the mesh, idontwant_message_size_threshold=1000). val0 (the RPC node) flood-publishes each 128 KB native batch straight to val1 and val2. On receipt, `handle_received_message` (behaviour.rs:1764-1835) sends IDONTWANT (line 1795), then checks the duplicate cache (1825), then `forward_msg` (2713) forwards to every mesh/explicit peer except propagation_source and message.source: val1 forwards val0's batch to val2 and val2 forwards it to val1. The IDONTWANT cannot win the race on a LAN because the forward is issued inside the same handler call that received the message, microseconds after val0's two sends. Each duplicate arrives as a full 128 KB frame that the codec decodes and, under ValidationMode::Strict (behaviour.rs:85; protocol.rs:305-312 sets verify_signature=true at decode), ed25519-verifies (SHA-512 over 128 KB plus verify, roughly 0.15-0.2 ms) BEFORE the behaviour's duplicate check drops it. Volume from the cell: val0 published 82,574 actions; val1 received 22,105 gossip messages vs val0's 6,009 (consensus only), so about 16,100 native batches per 300 s = 54 batches/s of ~128 KB = about 6.9 MB/s useful, and the same again as cross-forward duplicates per follower. On loopback the measurable cost is small: 54 dup/s x 0.2 ms = ~11 ms/s of swarm-thread time (~1%) plus 6.9 MB/s of extra QUIC decrypt, so on this devnet the gain is at most ~1% of matched/s. The real payoff is the production topology: with mesh_n=6 every validator receives each batch 1 (flood) + ~6 (mesh forwards) times, i.e. ~7x the useful native bandwidth (7 x 6.9 MB/s = 48 MB/s inbound per validator at today's load); `Ignore` collapses that to 1x. The forwarded duplicates also sit in the same non-priority per-peer send queue (512 deep, B3) as a follower-turned-leader's gossiped proposal, so on a 1 Gbps WAN each 128 KB dup ahead of a proposal adds ~1 ms of head-of-line delay.

ideas.title: Any connected peer can flood the native-action topic: bodies are written to the never-pruned DA store before signature verification, the inbound channel is unbounded, and rejections carry no peer penalty
ideas.area: torus-network native gossip ingest / torus-mempool add_native_action_from_gossip
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (1) Gate the native-topic arm (crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:1331-1400) on `message.source` being a validator-set peer (or a configured RPC-node allowlist) exactly as the consensus arm does with `should_drop_banned_gossip`/author checks, and add a per-AUTHOR bytes-per-second limiter for the topic (TxGossipState-style, keyed by author not forwarder). (2) Replace the unbounded `native_inbound` channel (crates/torus-network/src/bridge.rs:218) with a bounded one plus try_send and a dropped-counter, matching NativeGossipHandle's 8192-cap design. (3) In crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:482-497 move `mirror_to_da` AFTER the sender is authenticated for raw-gossip provenance (keep mirror-first only for the proposer-authenticated 0xFD push, which is the availability-vs-validity case the comment defends). (4) Feed mempool rejections (sender mismatch / sig failure) back into peer_scoring for the message author.
ideas.reasoning: Failure scenario: a peer that can dial a validator (kad runs in Server mode, behaviour.rs:203-206; connection_limits allow max_peers=100 with 80 inbound, config.rs:213; the only refusal is the ban list) subscribes to NATIVE_ACTION_TOPIC and publishes 128 KB batches of 1024 well-formed forged (Address, SignedNativeAction) pairs (~110-byte ClaimRewards actions with random signatures). On every validator: the swarm thread bincode-decodes all 1024 pairs (swarm.rs:1354-1368) and pushes them into an UNBOUNDED channel (bridge.rs:218); the ingest task (torus-node main.rs:641-690) caps rayon in-flight at 1024 and then ingests INLINE on the tokio task, which slows the drain but never pushes back on the swarm producer, so queue memory grows without bound. For each pair `add_native_action_from_gossip` calls `mirror_to_da` FIRST (lib.rs:482-484), so the garbage body is put into CF_NATIVE_PENDING, then pays an ecrecover (~100 us) that fails or mismatches; the Err is logged at debug and the author is never penalized (main.rs:671-675; only bincode-level malformation is penalized at swarm.rs:1398-1402). CF_NATIVE_PENDING is only ever deleted by NativeDaStore::remove (native_da.rs:204), which s64 #178 notes has no production caller, so every forged body is retained forever. Arithmetic: 9 verify threads x ~7k ecrecover/s = ~60k actions/s of ingest ceiling = ~60 batches/s = ~7.5 MB/s of attacker traffic saturates half of every validator's cores; above that, at say 40 MB/s (~310 batches/s, 320k pairs/s), the unbounded queue grows by (320k-60k) x ~200 B = ~50 MB/s (OOM in minutes) while RocksDB absorbs 60k x 110 B = ~6.6 MB/s of permanent garbage per validator (~570 GB/day). The swarm thread, which also carries consensus, spends ~2 ms per batch decoding, i.e. ~60% busy at 300 batches/s. No rate limit applies: `tx_rate_limit_per_peer` is only consulted on the TX_TOPIC path (swarm.rs:1419), and gossipsub peer scoring is not enabled (no with_peer_score in torus-network).

ideas.title: Followers re-clone and re-write to RocksDB every body the proposer pushes in the 0xFD bundle even though gossip already delivered and mirrored 100% of them
ideas.area: torus-mempool add_native_action_from_gossip / pre-proposal push ingest
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs add_native_action_from_gossip (482-527): compute `verified_cache_key` and probe `verified_sender` BEFORE `mirror_to_da`; on a cache hit skip the mirror (the body was already buffered/written when that cache entry was seeded, since seeding happens only after a successful insert that every public ingress path mirrors first) and go straight to admit_gossip so the pool's own dedup returns DuplicateNativeAction. For session-signed actions (no cache key) use a cheap `pool.contains(compute_action_hash(..))` probe instead. Optionally have the swarm 0xFD arm (swarm.rs:1481-1492) tag pairs with provenance so the presence check can also skip the nonce-window work.
ideas.reasoning: With gossip pre-spread on, the cell shows every follower already holds every body before the push: native_gossip_received_actions val1=val2=82,574 equals val0's published count, native_da_pull_requests_total=0, native_bundle_repushed_total=0. Yet the proposer still pushes the full 0xFD bundle (200 actions at cap 200; ~23.6 KB each: PlaceOrderParams = u64 market + bool + 2 x i128 FixedPoint + two u32 bincode enum tags + bool + Option<u64> = ~59 B x 400 orders) = ~4.7 MB per block to each follower. The swarm decodes it (swarm.rs:1481-1492) into the same inbound channel, so each pushed action runs add_native_action_from_gossip: `mirror_to_da` clones the 23.6 KB body into da_pending (lib.rs:811-837), which put_batch-es it (native_da.rs:87-110: keccak, bincode re-serialize, WriteBatch, db.write) every 128 bodies, then the trust-cache hit skips ecrecover and the pool insert returns DuplicateNativeAction. Per follower per block that is ~4.7 MB of clones plus ~4.7 MB of RocksDB writes (WAL + memtable) that are byte-identical to rows already present; over the cell ~315 follower-blocks x 4.7 MB = ~1.5 GB of duplicate writes per follower (cf_native_pending memtable 25 MB, pending compaction shows up in the metrics dump). Critical-path share: the bundle lands just before the CompactBlock and the tail of the 200 (up to 127 bodies, avg ~60, i.e. 1.4-3 MB) sits in da_pending until the 50 ms age flush or until `flush_da_mirrors` is called from get_native_da (lib.rs:643) inside validate_block's da_reconstruct on the hotstuff thread (s64 line 134 attributes 39-46 ms to 'a flush, a ~4 MB MultiGet and 200 decodes'). A 1.4-3 MB WriteBatch is ~5-15 ms at typical 200-300 MB/s memtable+WAL rates, i.e. ~1-2% of a ~640 ms view, plus ~15-45 ms of rayon-thread time per block that competes for the shared 18-core host.

ideas.title: ModifyOrder executes without an ownership check and mutates the book before its margin check fails
ideas.area: torus-bridge native_executor.rs / torus-core order_book.rs (ModifyOrder path)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3134-3138 dispatches `Self::exec_modify_order(ctx, *order_id, *new_price, *new_qty)` WITHOUT `sender`; `exec_modify_order` (5168-5232) loops every book and calls `book.modify_order` directly. Pass `sender` and add the same `order.trader != *sender` rejection that `exec_cancel_order` has at 4977-4985. 2) Validate `new_qty > 0` (and >= lot_size / tick alignment for `new_price`) BEFORE touching the book: `OrderBook::modify_order` (order_book.rs:702-771) assigns `replacement.remaining_qty = q` unconditionally on the cancel-and-reinsert path, so 0 or negative quantities are inserted. 3) Reorder exec_modify_order so the margin delta is computed and checked from `old_order` + requested fields first, and the book is modified only if the balance check passes; today `book.modify_order(...)` runs (5178), `dirty_books` is marked, and the 'insufficient margin for modify' error (5203-5211) returns with the order already changed and no margin reserved. Add tests: foreign-sender modify rejected; negative/zero qty rejected; failed-margin modify leaves the book untouched.
ideas.reasoning: Concrete attack (any funded account, or any Trading-scoped session key: torus-types lib.rs:215-219 lists ModifyOrder under Trading scope; no ingress filter exists for the variant): attacker reads a victim's resting bid id from getOpenOrders (torus.rs:1895), submits ModifyOrder{order_id: victim's, new_price: Some(2x market), new_qty: Some(huge)}. modify_order cancels and re-inserts the victim's order at the new price with NO matching pass (insert_order, order_book.rs:1185-1200, only appends to the level queue), so it rests crossed; the attacker then sells into it and the victim buys at 2x. If the victim lacks margin for the bigger notional, the executor still leaves the order modified (book changed at 5178, error returned at 5203) — an unfunded resting order. Second vector: new_qty = -X on one's own order: match_at_level (1042-1131) computes fill_qty = min(taker_remaining, maker_remaining) = negative and records a negative Fill, and in exec_modify_order the negative notional makes old_margin > new_margin, releasing `delta.min(bal.order_margin)` — i.e. up to the trader's ENTIRE order_margin (5214-5220), freeing collateral that backs other resting orders. This variant has existed unchanged since a2ccc73 (git log -S exec_modify_order) and ECON-AUDIT-3.4.4 / docs contain no mention of modify_order.

ideas.title: ModifyOrder with a price change never matches: crossed book and bypassed PostOnly/STP/reduce-only rules
ideas.area: torus-core order_book.rs modify_order
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In `OrderBook::modify_order` (crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:751-771) route the price-changed replacement through the same matching path as `place_order` (match_at_level via the 979/1012 loops, would_cross check at 1217, PostOnly rejection at 497, reduce-only and STP handling), instead of `self.insert_order(replacement.clone())`. Equivalent: implement price-modify as cancel + `place_order(PlaceOrderParams{..old, price: new, quantity: remaining})` preserving the old id only when it rests. Add a test 'modify bid above best ask fills immediately' and make `verify_invariants` (927-929) run in a debug assertion after modify in the executor's test harness.
ideas.reasoning: insert_order (1185-1200) only appends to the level queue and updates indexes; it never consults the opposite side. A trader who amends a bid from 99 to 101 while the best ask is 100 gets a resting bid at 101: best_bid (101) > best_ask (100). Consequences: (a) the amend, which should fill at 100, does not fill until some later opposite taker arrives, and then fills at 101 (worse for the amender by 1%); (b) getMarkPrice/mid consumers see a negative spread; (c) verify_invariants would panic (it is only wired into fuzz/determinism tests, so production silently carries the crossed state); (d) PostOnly, reduce-only and the per-trader cap are not re-evaluated for the new price. Combined with finding 1 this is the primitive that makes the forced-repricing attack profitable, but it is a defect for honest use on its own.

ideas.title: No batched cancel/modify: the 200-action cap makes cancel-heavy (market-maker) flow ~400x slower than placing
ideas.area: protocol: NativeAction variants, mempool selection, executor
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Add `CancelOrderBatch(Vec<OrderId>)` (and a `ModifyOrderBatch` or a mixed `OrderOps(Vec<OrderOp>)` of place/cancel/modify) under one signature + one nonce, mirroring PlaceOrderBatch: canonical tag 26+ in torus-types lib.rs append_canonical_bytes (684-895), an EIP-712 typehash in eip712.rs beside hash_place_order_batch (300-316), `batch_len_within_cap` reuse, Trading session-scope list (lib.rs:215-219), `is_cancel` in torus-mempool native_pool.rs:539 so the batch keeps cancel priority, ActionCategory in native_executor.rs:5988-6002, and an executor arm that calls the existing bounded batch primitive in crates/torus-core/src/order_book/cancel_batch.rs (`try_cancel_all_batch`, used by cancel_all at 649) with an explicit id list plus the ownership check from exec_cancel_order. Count it as one action under `native_per_block_cap`, with the per-block `orders_cap` charged per id.
ideas.reasoning: Capacity arithmetic from the measured cells: ~200 actions/block x 1.1 blk/s = 220 actions/s. A PlaceOrderBatch carries up to 1024 orders (NATIVE_ORDERS_PER_BATCH_CAP, lib.rs:513; bench uses 400), so placing runs at ~90k orders/s, but CancelOrder and ModifyOrder are one order per action, so the chain can retire at most ~220 individual orders/s — a 400x asymmetry. The only bulk primitive is CancelAllOrders (whole account or whole market), which is what the bench uses (cancel_fraction 0.05, all markets) precisely to stay under the book's MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET = 200 (order_book.rs:28, 411). A market maker quoting 200 levels on one market needs 200 CancelOrder actions — an entire block's cap — to requote selectively; with realistic MM flow (roughly one cancel per placed order) sustained throughput collapses to ~220 orders/s, i.e. >99% below the 60-65k matched/s headline, and place batches from other senders are starved by the cancels-first sort (native_pool.rs:390). The exec side already has an O(n) batched removal (cancel_batch.rs) so the book cost of a 400-id cancel batch is comparable to the measured cancel-all pass.

ideas.reasoning: Bytes today (bincode 1 fixint, the format used by `bincode::serialize`): market_id u64 8 + is_buy 1 + price i128 16 + quantity i128 16 + OrderType tag u32 4 + TimeInForce tag u32 4 + reduce_only 1 + Option tag 1 = 51 B/order; a 400-order action = 4+8+20,400+8+4+65 = 20,489 B; 200 actions/block = 4.10 MB, which matches the s64 doc's '~4 MB durable body write (commit_persist 45-54 ms)' and 'one ~4 MB keccak pass ... 15 ms'. Canonical preimage is 45 B/order = 3.6 MB/block keccak'd on the commit path (action hash + verified_cache_key restash, s64 #4: ~30+15 ms). Compact layout: 8+8+2+1 = 19 B/order (27 with coid) -> 1.52 MB/block (-63%); a varint price (6e12 raw fits 6 B) gives ~10 B (-80%). Costs that scale with body bytes on the next leader's critical path per s64: commit_persist ~50 ms, keccak passes ~15 ms, da_reconstruct MultiGet+decode 39-46 ms partially, gossip encode/decode. Proportional saving ~ (50+15+~20)*0.63 ≈ 50 ms of a ~640 ms view ≈ 8% if all remain on the path; s64 #1/#5/#10 aim to move most of it off-thread, so the residual after those land is ~1-3%. Rate-limit comments assume ~70-150 B/order (rate_limit.rs:241-247), so the 12 MB bytes cap is not binding either way.

ideas.title: Cancel/modify by client_order_id: today an order cannot be cancelled until it is committed, executed and polled
ideas.area: protocol/API: CancelOrder, ModifyOrder, order_book indexes, RPC
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Add `CancelByClientId { market_id, client_order_id }` (and the same key for modify/replace) as NativeAction variants (canonical tag, EIP-712 typehash, Trading scope, is_cancel, ActionCategory as for CancelOrder). In OrderBook maintain `HashMap<(Address, u64), OrderId>` updated in insert_order (order_book.rs:1185-1200), cancel_order (590), cancel_all/try_cancel_all_batch and the fill/STP removals in match_at_level (1078-1131); reject a duplicate resting coid per trader at place time so the key is unique. Executor arm: resolve to OrderId then reuse exec_cancel_order (ownership implicit via the sender-keyed lookup).
ideas.reasoning: OrderIds are allocated at execution (`alloc_id`, order_book.rs:373) from a global counter whose value depends on the order's position among all senders' orders in the block, so a client cannot compute its id. Under CTE the id exists only after commit (~1.5 views x ~640 ms ≈ 1 s), exec (which lags commit; the pool has exec-backlog pacing tiers, native_pool.rs:1231), and a getOpenOrders poll (torus.rs:193, which is the only place client_order_id is surfaced, 1895). The earliest a maker can pull or amend a quote is therefore ~2 block intervals after sending it (~2 s at 1.1 blk/s), and every cancel/replace cycle costs a full extra round trip plus RPC polling. client_order_id is already signed, hashed, persisted in book rows (order_book.rs:2280-2495) and capped per trader (200/market), but nothing indexes it. With cancel-by-coid a maker signs the cancel at place time and it lands in the next block (cancels sort first in the pool, native_pool.rs:390, so it must not share a block with its place), halving quote time-at-risk and removing the getOpenOrders polling.

ideas.expected_improvement: cancel/amend round trip from >=2 block intervals + poll (~2-3 s) to 1 block interval (~0.9 s); no throughput change on the current bench
ideas.risk: Consensus format change; duplicate-coid rule must be deterministic and enforced identically at ingress and exec; index maintenance must cover every removal path (fills, STP, cancel-all, liquidation) or the lookup goes stale.
ideas.why_new: Prior rounds treat order identity only via chain OrderId; no doc or memory mentions cancel-by-client-id or the exec-time id allocation latency.

ideas.title: Header-first pipeline never validates TC/NEC or reproposal and never writes LOCAL_TIP — MonadBFT tail-fork resistance is dead code on the live path
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs/hotstuff/implementation.rs (on_receive_proposal_header, broadcast_proposal_as_header), pacemaker TimeoutVote
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) In `on_receive_proposal_header` (crates/hotstuff_rs/src/hotstuff/implementation.rs:1871-2130) port the checks that only exist in `on_receive_proposal` (lines 1071-1117): if `header.nec` is Some run `valid_nec`; if `!has_valid_nec && header.tc.is_some_and(|tc| tc.high_tip_is_winner)` require `tc.is_correct(block_tree) && view == tc.view+1 && tc.high_tip.block_hash == header.block_hash`, else drop. 2) After the header vote (line ~2098 `set_vote_state_atomic`) call `block_tree.set_local_tip(TipInfo{block_hash, height, justify, data_hash, view})` for fresh proposals and `set_local_tip(tc.high_tip)` for reproposals, mirroring lines 1257-1275 — or fold LOCAL_TIP into `set_vote_state_atomic` so it is written in the same batch as LAST_VOTED_PROPOSAL. 3) Add a regression test in the style of header_fast_path_regression_test.rs: leader after a TC with `high_tip_is_winner=true` proposes a different block via header; replicas must NOT vote.
ideas.reasoning: All four leader send sites emit headers only: implementation.rs:551, 568, 713, 1695 call `broadcast_proposal_as_header` (762-797, `header.into()` on 782); the only full `Proposal` broadcast left is the NEC path at 1854. `ProposalHeader` carries `tc` and `nec` (messages.rs:419-420) but the entire header handler (1871-2370) contains zero reads of `header.tc`, `header.nec`, `is_reproposal`, `valid_nec`, `high_tip` or `set_local_tip` (verified by scanning that range). `set_local_tip` is called only at 1267, 1272 (on_receive_proposal) and 1371 (nudge), and `set_vote_state_atomic` (block_tree/accessors/internal.rs:645) does not touch LOCAL_TIP. Consequences: (a) honest validators' LOCAL_TIP is never written, so every TimeoutVote (pacemaker/implementation.rs:136,161,324 read `block_tree.local_tip()`) carries `local_tip: None`; the TimeoutVoteCollector (pacemaker/types.rs:203-216) therefore never sets `high_tip`, `high_tip_is_winner` is always false, `create_proposal_based_on_tc` (implementation.rs:788-798) never reproposes, and NECollector/RECOVER/NERequest/NE/valid_nec (~500 lines) are unreachable in production. (b) Even if a TC did say `high_tip_is_winner`, replicas on the header path would vote for whatever the next leader sends. Concrete failure: view v: leader proposes X, replicas vote (votes persisted, block-tree LAST_VOTED_PROPOSAL=X), the vote collector may even form QC(X) (implementation.rs:1452) but the view times out before the next header lands (the bench sees 120-170 timeouts/node/300 s). Leader of v+1 extends its own highest QC (X's parent) with a fresh block Y; every replica votes Y; X and its up-to-200 actions are abandoned and must be re-proposed or expire (35% of offered actions already expire). This is exactly the tail-fork MonadBFT's reproposal rule exists to prevent; at n=3 it is a throughput/fairness loss, with a Byzantine leader at n>=4 it is a deliberate censorship/tail-fork of any QC'd-but-not-yet-extended block.
