ideas.title: TimeoutVote/TC/NE signatures bind only a fraction of what the protocol acts on — one Byzantine validator can force RECOVER every timeout and halt the chain
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs pacemaker/messages.rs, pacemaker/types.rs, hotstuff/types.rs, hotstuff/implementation.rs (NE/NEC path)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) `TimeoutVote::build_message_bytes` (pacemaker/messages.rs:137-153): sign the full TipInfo (block_hash, height, view, data_hash, hash of block_justify) and the full highest_qc hash, not just tip.block_hash + (qc.view, qc.block); extend `voter_metadata` (pacemaker/types.rs:56) to carry tip.view. 2) In `TimeoutVoteCollector::collect` (pacemaker/types.rs:187-247) and `TimeoutCertificate::is_correctly_signed` (89-146): verify `local_tip.block_justify.is_correct` and `highest_qc.is_correct` before they can become `high_tip`/`high_qc`, and on TC verification recompute `high_tip`/`high_qc`/`high_tip_is_winner` from `voter_metadata` and reject a TC whose fields disagree. 3) Bind NE signatures to `(chain_id, view, high_tip.block_hash, high_tip_qc_view)` (implementation.rs:1741, types.rs:376) and verify `req.tc.is_correct` in `on_receive_ne_request` (1707). 4) In the NEC fresh-proposal path (implementation.rs:1806-1840) require `high_tip_qc.is_correct(block_tree)` and a known parent, and on failure keep `recovery_state` so the leader can fall back to extending its own highest_pc instead of silently not proposing.
ideas.reasoning: The audit item 'unsigned TimeoutVote tip fields' (docs/Torus-hyperBFT-review.md:315) was fixed only partially: the signature covers `(chain_id, view, tip.block_hash, qc.view, qc.block)` (messages.rs:137-153). Unsigned but acted upon: `tip.view` (decides `high_tip` and `high_tip_is_winner`, types.rs:210-227), `tip.block_justify` (becomes the justify of the NEC fresh block at implementation.rs:1807-1840 and `high_tip_qc_view` for NE signatures at 1740), `tip.height`, `tip.data_hash`; nobody recomputes `Block::hash(height, justify, data_hash)` for a TipInfo (only headers get that check at 1929). At TC level `is_correctly_signed` verifies voter signatures but never checks that `high_tip`/`high_qc`/`high_tip_is_winner` were derived from `voter_metadata`, so any relayer (AdvanceView, `highest_tc` inside timeout votes, proposal.tc) can rewrite them and the TC still passes `is_correct`. The nested PCs `tc.high_qc` and `tc.high_tip.block_justify` are never signature-verified anywhere. NE signatures cover only `(view, high_tip_qc_view)` — no chain_id, no block hash — so an NEC obtained against phantom tip P is equally valid against any real tip X with the same justify view, and `on_receive_ne_request` does not verify `req.tc` at all. Concrete scenario (n=4, f=1, once finding 1 is fixed or with the code as-is since honest local_tips are None): whenever a view v times out, Byzantine validator B broadcasts TimeoutVote{local_tip: TipInfo{block_hash: random, view: v, block_justify: <arbitrary QC with unknown block>}}. Signature check passes (only block_hash is bound); CONS-FIND-26 (`tip.view > current` -> drop, pacemaker/implementation.rs:344) passes since tip.view == v; the collector picks it as high_tip (honest tips are None or older), `high_tip_is_winner = v > qc_view` = true. Next honest leader: `create_proposal_based_on_tc` -> block absent -> Case 5 RECOVER (804-880); honest validators never voted for the phantom so all send NE (1722-1770); NEC forms; leader takes `tip.block_justify` as justify, `block_height(pb)` returns None -> `BlockExpectedButNotFound` -> error logged and message dropped (algorithm.rs:305-313), `recovery_state` already reset to None (1801) -> no proposal in v+1 -> timeout -> B repeats. One Byzantine validator (within f) turns every timeout into a permanent halt; alternatively B supplies a genuine-but-old QC and each timeout costs an extra RECOVER round trip (ProposalRequest + NERequest + NE + full Proposal broadcast, ~3 message delays) before progress.

ideas.title: ed25519 signature-set certificates cost O(n^2) verifies per view (AdvanceView re-verification + nested TCs) and O(n) bytes — fine at n=3, breaks max_view_time around n~60-100
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs types (SignatureSet/PhaseCertificate/TimeoutCertificate), pacemaker on_receive_advance_view / on_receive_timeout_vote
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Ladder, cheapest first: (1) In `on_receive_advance_view` (pacemaker/implementation.rs:453-479) skip `pc.is_correct` when `pc == block_tree.highest_pc()` or `pc.view <= highest_pc.view` (byte-equality is enough: the PC is already trusted), and in `on_receive_timeout_vote` (line 340) skip `highest_tc.is_correct` when `tc.view <= block_tree.highest_tc().view`; keep a per-view HashSet<(view, block, phase)> of already-verified certificates. This turns n^2 into ~n verifies per view with no format change. (2) Replace the per-signature loops in `PhaseCertificate::is_correctly_signed` (hotstuff/types.rs:150-190), `TimeoutCertificate::is_correctly_signed` (pacemaker/types.rs:89-146) and `is_nec_correctly_signed` (types.rs:369-396) with `ed25519_dalek::verify_batch` — the `batch` feature is already enabled workspace-wide (Cargo.toml:131) and already used at crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1164; also hoist the `try_to_vec()`/`base_msg.clone()` out of the loop. (3) Only when the validator set is planned to exceed ~30: move certificates to BLS12-381 aggregate signatures (blst) with a signer bitmap, keeping ed25519 for peer identity; this is a consensus/wire-format change and slower than ed25519 at n=3.
ideas.reasoning: Per view, every validator broadcasts AdvanceView(PC) (pacemaker/implementation.rs:194-215, once per view when highest_pc.view >= cur_view) and the vote collector broadcasts another on PC formation (hotstuff/implementation.rs:1549-1556). Each receipt runs `pc.is_correct` unconditionally (pacemaker/implementation.rs:475), which is a loop of `signer.verify` over the whole SignatureSet (hotstuff/types.rs:161-181) — n ed25519 verifies — before any comparison with the already-known highest_pc. Plus the header's justify (implementation.rs:1958) = n more. Per view per node: ~n*(n-1)+n = n^2 verifies. With ~50 us per ed25519-dalek verify (unmeasured on this host; dalek 2.2/curve25519 4.1.3, Cargo.lock:2046,1791): n=3 -> 9 verifies = 0.45 ms = 0.07% of a 620 ms view (no measurable gain from any change here at n=3); n=25 -> 625 = 31 ms = 6% of the 500 ms max_view_time (torus-node/src/main.rs:314,799); n=64 -> 4096 = 205 ms = 41%; n=100 -> 10,000 = 500 ms = 100% of max_view_time on the single hotstuff-algo thread, i.e. every view times out from certificate verification alone. Timeout rounds are worse: each of the n-1 TimeoutVotes embeds `highest_tc` which is re-verified (n verifies, 2n during a validator-set transition, pacemaker/types.rs:70-84) and each AdvanceView(TC) is verified again (n) -> ~2n^2: n=100 -> 20,000 verifies = 1.0 s per timeout round > max_view_time, so timeouts cascade. Wire size (borsh: ChainID 8, ViewNumber 8, CryptoHash 32, Phase 1, Vec<Option<[u8;64]>> = 4 + 65n; data_types.rs:167,328): PC = 53+65n B (n=3: 248 B; n=100: 6.6 KB); TC = sigs + voter_metadata (74n) + high_tip TipInfo (80 B + PC) + high_qc PC ~ 294+269n B (n=100: 27 KB); TimeoutVote = 80 B + TC + TipInfo + PC ~ 560+399n B (n=100: 40 KB), broadcast all-to-all -> n(n-1) x 40 KB = ~400 MB per timeout round network-wide at n=100 (4 MB egress per node). A BLS aggregate certificate would be 96 B + n/8 bitmap (n=100: ~160 B, 40x smaller) but costs ~1.2-1.5 ms per verification (2 pairings + n point adds), i.e. ~10x slower than 3 ed25519 verifies at n=3 and break-even only around n~25-30 — so the O(n^2) redundancy (step 1) is the actual scaling defect, not the scheme.

ideas.title: Session expiry is never enforced on the consensus path (seconds vs milliseconds)
ideas.area: torus-types eip712.rs batch_verify_impl/resolve_sender; torus-consensus app.rs exec + validate; torus-bridge validator.rs/proposer.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Every consensus-path session resolver passes the block header timestamp (SECONDS, app.rs:4633-4636 `.as_secs()`) into a check that compares it with `SessionData.expiry` (MILLISECONDS): eip712.rs:1143 `timestamp <= session.expiry` (called from app.rs:1647-1650 exec and app.rs:4492-4495 validate) and eip712.rs:826 `current_timestamp > session.expiry` (called from validator.rs:370 and proposer.rs:210). Fix: convert once at the boundary (`header.timestamp.saturating_mul(1000)`, the same convention exec_create_session already uses at native_executor.rs:5417 `now_ms = ctx.timestamp.saturating_mul(1000)`), or add a `header_timestamp_ms()` helper on TorusBlockHeader and use it at all four call sites. Add a unit test: session with expiry = 1_700_000_000_000 (ms) and a seconds timestamp of 1_700_000_001 must resolve to None. This is a consensus validity change: lockstep deploy across the fleet.
ideas.reasoning: A seconds timestamp is ~1.76e9; a millisecond expiry is ~1.76e12, so `secs <= expiry_ms` is true for every session created before ~year 2100 and `secs > expiry_ms` is never true. The 24h MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS bound (eip712.rs:736) and any client-chosen shorter expiry are therefore enforced ONLY at RPC ingress (torus.rs:300 uses wall-clock ms) and never by consensus. Concrete failure: a hot session key with a 1h expiry leaks; after the hour the RPC rejects it ('session key expired'), but an attacker who gossips the signed action directly to a validator (main.rs:671 -> add_native_action_from_gossip, mempool lib.rs:505-517, which checks signature and session existence but not expiry) gets it admitted, selected, and executed by every node, because exec re-resolves with the seconds timestamp. The same holds for a Byzantine leader including expired-session actions: validate (app.rs:4492) and exec (app.rs:1647) both accept them. Only an explicit EIP-712 RevokeSession closes the window. The existing tests never catch this because make_session uses expiry u64::MAX (eip712.rs:1555-1561) and the session_key_tests only cover the CreateSession side of the unit bug.

ideas.title: count_sessions_for_owner is a full CF scan that also counts expired sessions: O(N) exec-thread stall and permanent 5-session lockout
ideas.area: torus-state db.rs/backend.rs count_sessions_for_owner; torus-bridge native_executor.rs exec_create_session
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (1) Replace the scan with an owner index: on put_session/delete_session also write/delete a row keyed owner(20B)||pubkey(32B) in a new CF (or a prefix of CF_SESSIONS) so the count is a prefix iteration over at most 5 rows; or keep a per-owner count row updated in the same atomic batch. (2) Make the cap count ACTIVE sessions: skip rows whose expiry <= now_ms in the count, and let exec_create_session overwrite an expired row for the same pubkey (currently 'session key already exists' at native_executor.rs:5439-5445). (3) Optionally prune expired rows lazily on the next CreateSession by that owner. Files: crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:678-692, crates/torus-state/src/backend.rs:85-95 (trait default used by NativeStateOverlay at exec), crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5424-5450.
ideas.reasoning: At exec, ctx.state is the NativeStateOverlay, so the trait DEFAULT count_sessions_for_owner runs (backend.rs:85-95): iterate_cf(CF_SESSIONS, None) materializes EVERY session row as owned (Vec<u8>,Vec<u8>) pairs and serde_json-decodes each one, per CreateSession, on the single exec thread. Arithmetic: 50k users x 5 sessions = 250k rows; ~1 us JSON decode + 2 allocs per row => ~0.25-0.5 s per CreateSession. A block at cap 200 filled with CreateSession actions (5000 gas each, native_executor.rs:5460) costs 200 x 0.25-0.5 s = 50-100 s of exec-thread time: with CTE the chain keeps committing but exec falls arbitrarily behind (app.rs:8823 comment says exec lags commit arbitrarily), and every node repeats it. This is a cheap, permissionless DoS that grows with adoption. Separately, the count includes expired sessions and nothing ever deletes them except an EIP-712 RevokeSession from the owner; the bench author already hit this (main.rs:1333-1338: 'expired sessions still count toward the max-5-per-owner cap (count_sessions_for_owner does not filter by expiry)' and had to add a revoke-then-create phase). Concrete failure: a wallet that creates a fresh 24h session each day gets 'max 5 active sessions exceeded' on day 6 with zero active sessions, and clients that lost the old session pubkeys cannot recover without a chain-side change. The error string says 'active' but the code counts all rows.

crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:676-692 (StateDb version: iterator over the whole CF; comment 'acceptable since ... total count is bounded' is not true: nothing bounds it)

crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5424-5450 (cap check then 'already exists' reject; no expiry filtering)

crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:736-739 (24h max expiry, 5 per address)
ideas.expected_improvement: prevents an O(total sessions) exec-thread stall per CreateSession (50-100 s per full block at 250k sessions) and the day-6 lockout of session-key users
ideas.risk: Changing what the cap counts is consensus-visible (an old node counts expired rows, a new one does not) -> lockstep deploy. The index CF is a schema addition; needs a migration/backfill for existing sessions or a fresh genesis.
ideas.why_new: No perf doc or exploration entry mentions count_sessions_for_owner or session state growth; the only prior acknowledgement is the bench workaround comment.

ideas.title: Session actions miss the parallel Phase-1 verify: struct hashing + ed25519 batch run serially on the exec/validate thread
ideas.area: torus-types eip712.rs batch_verify_impl (Phase 2)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In batch_verify_impl (eip712.rs:1092-1177) move the pure per-action work for session actions into the parallel Phase 1 map: compute `eip712_signing_hash(domain, eip712_struct_hash(&action.action, action.nonce))` and `Ed25519VerifyingKey::from_bytes` for every ActionSignature::Session action inside recover_senders_phase1 (return an enum {Eip712(Option<Address>), Session{hash, vk}} per index), keeping only the session_lookup/expiry/scope filter and the final verify_batch sequential. Optionally split verify_batch into chunks of ~32 and run them via par_iter in the same pool so the ed25519 cost is also parallel. Add a differential test that the result vector is byte-identical to the current implementation for mixed batches.
ideas.reasoning: For an EIP-712 action the keccak struct hash AND the ecrecover run inside the rayon map (recover_senders_phase1, eip712.rs:959-1005). For a session action Phase 1 returns None (eip712.rs:975) and Phase 2 (eip712.rs:1130-1160) recomputes eip712_struct_hash sequentially, then verify_batch runs single-threaded (eip712.rs:1162-1174). For the bench's PlaceOrderBatch of 400 orders, hash_place_order_batch (eip712.rs:303-316) is 400 x keccak(320 B) + keccak(12.8 KB): 400 x ~3 permutations x ~0.25 us ~= 0.3 ms plus ~95 permutations ~= 25 us, so ~0.33 ms per batch action; at cap 200 that is ~65 ms of serial keccak per block on the exec thread, plus ~6 ms for verify_batch of 200 signatures (~30 us amortized each). The EIP-712 equivalent (200 x ~120 us ecrecover + the same hashing) is ~90 ms of CPU but spread over the rayon pool (9+ workers on the 18-core host) -> ~10 ms wall. So today the 'fast path' session mode is ~7x SLOWER on the exec critical section than EIP-712 mode at cap 200 with 400-order batches, and the same serial cost hits validate_body_checks_core (app.rs:4492) on non-attested blocks. Hoisting the hashing makes session-mode exec verify ~65 ms -> ~8 ms per block. Caveat: the s65 cells ran EIP-712 mode (bench.log has no session lines), so this cost is not in the measured 60-65k matched/s; the gain is realized only when clients use session keys, which is the intended production path (eip712.rs:705-709).

ideas.title: Gossip ingest of session actions skips scope, requires_eip712 and expiry checks that RPC ingress enforces
ideas.area: torus-mempool lib.rs add_native_action_from_gossip
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: At crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:505-517 replace the `verify_session_signature()` + `self.state.get_session(&pubkey)` pair with `action.resolve_sender(now_ms, |pk| self.state.get_session(pk).ok().flatten())` (now_ms from the same SystemTime read admit_gossip already does), so the gossip path applies the same requires_eip712 (eip712.rs:814), expiry (826) and scope (829) rules as the RPC path (torus.rs:300 validate_with_sessions). Add a mempool test: a Trading-scoped session signing NativeAction::Withdraw must be rejected at gossip ingest.
ideas.reasoning: RPC ingress rejects a session-signed action whose scope does not allow it, that requires EIP-712 (Withdraw, Delegate, CreateSession...), or whose session is expired. The gossip path only checks that the ed25519 signature verifies and that the session row exists and resolves to the claimed sender. Concrete failure: any peer holding a legitimately registered Trading-scope session key gossips session-signed Withdraw/Delegate/CancelAll-for-other-market actions; every validator admits them (they pass 'gossip sender mismatch'), DA-mirrors them (lib.rs:487), and the proposer selects them into blocks where each consumes one of the 200 cap slots; at exec they resolve to None (eip712.rs:1138 requires_eip712 / 1143 scope) and are dropped with a per-action warn (app.rs:1726-1734). With the pool already over capacity (~343 actions/s offered vs ~225/s included), each such action displaces a valid one, so an attacker converts cheap ed25519 signatures into lost block capacity at up to 512 per sender per pool (NATIVE_PER_SENDER_CAP, rate_limit.rs:167). Combined with the expiry bug above, actions from expired sessions are not merely admitted but executed.
evidence: crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:505-517 (gossip session path: verify_session_signature + get_session only)
crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:770-790 (verify_session_signature doc: 'Does NOT check session state (expiry, scope)')
crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:814-832 (resolve_sender: requires_eip712, expiry, scope)
crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:299-303 (RPC path uses validate_with_sessions)
crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:665-675 (gossip topic feeds add_native_action_from_gossip)
crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1722-1734 (dropped at exec, one warn per action)
ideas.expected_improvement: prevents a peer from filling block cap slots with session actions that are guaranteed to be dropped at exec; closes the ingress/consensus policy gap
ideas.risk: Node-local admission change only (not consensus-visible). A session created in a block that is committed but not yet applied on this node would be rejected at gossip exactly as it already is at RPC.
ideas.why_new: The gossip re-verification angle in the parallel round covers ecrecover/trust-cache cost, not the missing session policy checks; no doc mentions this gap.

ideas.title: Multiple session keys of one owner share a millisecond nonce space: same-ms actions from different keys are silently dropped at exec
ideas.area: torus-consensus app.rs exec replay guard; torus-state cf.rs native_nonce_key; mempool native_pool.rs dedup
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Either (a) namespace the replay key by signer for session actions: native_nonce_key(owner, nonce) -> key = owner || session_pubkey_prefix || nonce (or a 1-byte signer tag), applied identically at app.rs:1735, validator.rs:376 and proposer.rs:214, with the mempool per-sender dedup unchanged; or (b) keep one owner nonce space but reject the collision at RPC ingress (the pool can check its own (owner, nonce) index at insert, native_pool.rs:186-219 currently dedups only on (sender, action_hash)) so the client gets an error instead of a silent drop; and document that clients must use strictly increasing per-owner nonces across all their session keys. Option (b) is node-local and cheap; (a) is consensus-visible.
ideas.reasoning: MAX_SESSIONS_PER_ADDRESS = 5 exists so one owner can run several independent signers (bots). Each signs with nonce = wall-clock ms (bench main.rs:293-318, 395-400 describe this as the expected client scheme). A session action resolves to `session.owner` (eip712.rs:832, 1156), and the exec replay guard keys on (owner, nonce) (app.rs:1735-1748 native_nonce_key(&sender, signed.nonce)), so two different session keys of the same owner that sign in the same millisecond collide: the pool admits both (dedup is by (sender, action_hash) which commits to the signature, native_pool.rs:186-189, lib.rs:947-952), the RPC returns an ack hash for both, and at exec the second is skipped with 'skipping duplicate/replayed native action' (app.rs:1741-1747) and never executed. Arithmetic: two bots each at 20 actions/s with ms nonces: P(other bot has an action in the same ms) ~ 20/1000 = 2% per action -> ~0.8 silently lost actions/s per owner; at bench-like rates (hundreds/s per owner) it is tens per second. Nothing surfaces this to the client except a validator warn log. The bench never sees it because it registers exactly one session per sender (main.rs:1294-1315).

crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:92-97 (native_nonce_key = sender||nonce)

crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:939-952 (action hash commits to session pubkey + sig, so both copies are distinct)
tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:293-318, 1294-1315 (ms nonces; one session per sender)

ideas.expected_improvement: prevents silent loss of ~2% of actions per pair of same-owner session keys at 20 actions/s each (scales with rate); acked-but-never-executed orders
ideas.risk: Option (a) changes the nonce-key layout (consensus-visible, needs lockstep deploy and affects the same key used by EIP-712 actions unless tagged); option (b) adds an index lookup per pool insert but no consensus change.
ideas.why_new: No prior doc discusses multi-session-key clients; the s64 list and the in-progress FIFO/admission work treat nonces per sender only.

ideas.title: run_liquidation_checks force-closes every market's positions at the loop market's oracle price and tier config
ideas.area: torus-bridge/native_executor.rs run_liquidation_checks + torus-core/liquidation.rs check_liquidations
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5747-5795, the per-market loop calls LiquidationEngine::check_liquidations(&ctx.positions, traders, config, oracle_prices) which returns Liquidation entries for ALL of a trader's markets (liquidation.rs:80-109: cross accounts flag every cross position, isolated positions of every market are appended), then executes each with `oracle_price` looked up for the LOOP's `*market_id` (L5762-5775) and runs ADL in `*market_id` (L5782-5788), not `liq.market_id`. Fix: (1) look the price up per `liq.market_id` inside the execute loop and pass `liq.market_id` to auto_deleverage; (2) make check_liquidations/total_maintenance_margin take a per-market config map (`&HashMap<MarketId, MarketMarginConfig>`) so margin.rs:202-229 uses each position's own market tiers instead of one market's; (3) run the trader scan once, not once per market config. Add a test with two cross positions in markets 1 and 2 and assert each is closed at its own price.
ideas.reasoning: Concrete failure: trader has cross positions BTC (market 1, long 1 @ 50,000) and ETH (market 2, short 1 @ 3,000); prices (1: 48,500), (2: 3,500); balance 500. Loop market_id=1: check_liquidations flags BOTH (the existing test crates/torus-core/tests/liquidation_tests.rs:165-194 `cross_margin_multiple_positions` asserts liqs.len()==2 with a single config). execute_liquidation(ETH liq, oracle_price=48,500): pnl = (3,000-48,500)*1 = -45,500; penalty = 48,500*2.5% = 1,212.5 to the insurance fund; balance -> deficit ~46,000 -> auto_deleverage(market 1, 46,000, 48,500) deleverages BTC counterparties for an ETH loss. The true ETH loss was 500. Also total_maintenance_margin (margin.rs:216-225) sizes every position with market 1's tier table. Today the pipeline never calls run_liquidation_checks (app.rs:1889-1892 calls drain_core_writer/process_governance/distribute_fees/process_epoch_boundary only) and ctx.margin_configs is only ever HashMap::new() (native_executor.rs:1869), which is a known finding; what is new is that the moment it is wired with >1 market it liquidates at wrong prices, so it cannot be enabled as-is.

ideas.title: Wiring liquidation checks as written costs ~150k overlay prefix scans per block (~1-5 s) — would stall execution
ideas.area: torus-core/liquidation.rs + margin.rs + torus-state overlay iterate_cf
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Before enabling run_liquidation_checks: (1) collapse the 3 prefix scans per (market, trader) into one `positions_for_trader` per trader per block (check_liquidations L81, cross_margin_equity margin.rs:185, total_maintenance_margin margin.rs:208 each re-scan), and drop the outer per-market loop; (2) restrict the candidate set to traders touched this block (fills, balance changes) plus, per market whose mark moved, positions whose liquidation price is crossed — keep a per-market `BTreeMap<liq_price, (trader)>` (or a sorted Vec) in the resident state next to the books, updated in pass B of settle where positions are already written; (3) give the overlay a range-bounded iterate (BTreeMap::range on `writes` instead of `starts_with` over all pending entries, backend.rs:320-333) so a prefix scan is O(hits) not O(pending).
ideas.reasoning: Arithmetic from the s65-zerocode-r270-r3 cell and the code: senders N=5,000 (summary.json), markets M=10 (bench_cmd --markets 10), every executor position is MarginType::Cross (native_executor.rs:4508/4579/4891/4905 hard-code Cross) so `has_cross` is true for every trader. Per (market config, trader) the code does 3 `positions_for_trader` prefix scans + 1 balance read. Scans/block = 10 x 5,000 x 3 = 150,000. Each overlay scan (backend.rs:1114-1137) does a RocksDB prefix seek with no prefix extractor configured (no `prefix_extractor` in torus-state) plus `overlay_into` for the parent layer and own layer, each doing `starts_with` over ALL pending writes+deletes of cf_native_positions. Pending positions/block = torus_exec_dirty_entries_positions_total / torus_exec_engine_seconds_count = 1,146,946 / 454 = 2,526 (metrics-after-val1.txt); with the pipeline parent layer ~5k entries filtered per scan, ~20 us, plus seek ~5-15 us and Vec/BTreeMap allocs => ~30-40 us/scan. 150,000 x 35 us = ~5.3 s per block; even the seek-only floor 150,000 x 5 us = 0.75 s, i.e. about one full block interval (1.1 native blocks/s). Plus deriving `traders` needs a full cf_native_positions scan (~50k rows, ~6 MB copy) since no trader index CF exists (torus-state/src/cf.rs). The post-engine tail is serial on the exec thread (app.rs:1888-1892), so this directly adds to exec time per block and would cut matched/s by well over half.

ideas.title: Cross-margin liquidation is executed per leg: a losing leg's deficit is ADL'd away before the winning leg's profit is paid back to the liquidated trader
ideas.area: torus-core/liquidation.rs execute_liquidation + native_executor.rs run_liquidation_checks
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Make cross-margin liquidation account-level: in run_liquidation_checks group Liquidation entries by trader, close all cross legs, sum PnL and penalties, apply to the balance once, and compute `remaining_deficit` from the account total (liquidation.rs:221-241 currently does the deficit test per position and zeroes the balance per position). Only then run ADL/insurance for the account-level deficit. Add a test: cross account with legs (-10,000) and (+6,000), balance 1,000, market ids ordered so the loser is closed first, assert no ADL fires and the trader ends at 0.
ideas.reasoning: execute_liquidation (liquidation.rs:193-252) reads the balance, adds this leg's pnl minus penalty, and if negative sets available=0 and reports the shortfall as `remaining_deficit`; the executor then calls auto_deleverage for that deficit (native_executor.rs:5781-5788). Legs are processed in prefix-scan order (market_id ascending, position key = trader||market_id BE, position.rs:202-207, merged BTreeMap in backend.rs:1129). Scenario: balance 1,000, market 1 leg upnl -10,000, market 2 leg upnl +6,000, account equity = -3,000. Leg 1: 1,000 - 10,000 - penalty -> deficit ~9,000+penalty, balance zeroed, ADL deleverages market-1 counterparties for ~9,000. Leg 2: 0 + 6,000 - penalty_2 -> the trader walks away with ~6,000 - penalty. Correct outcome: deficit 3,000 (+penalties), trader ends at 0. With the reverse market ordering the result is correct, so the outcome depends on which market id is smaller — non-economic and gameable (open the hedge in the higher market id). Value leaked = min(winning-leg profit, losing-leg deficit) per event.

ideas.title: ADL pays counterparties full mark PnL and socialize_loss is never called, so every liquidation deficit becomes unbacked balance
ideas.area: torus-core/liquidation.rs auto_deleverage / socialize_loss; native_executor.rs run_liquidation_checks
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (1) In auto_deleverage (liquidation.rs:255-342) close counterparties at the bankruptcy price of the liquidated position (entry +/- (balance+isolated_margin)/size), credit them `bankruptcy_pnl` rather than `unrealized_pnl(oracle)`, and reduce `loss_amount` by the difference (mark PnL - bankruptcy PnL) that the counterparty forgoes — that is what actually funds the deficit. (2) In run_liquidation_checks (native_executor.rs:5781-5789) stop discarding the ADL result (`let _ =`): take the insurance fund first (socialize_loss already implements fund-then-spread, L345-429, but has no caller outside tests), then ADL, then socialize the remainder, and emit a metric/log for any residual protocol deficit. (3) Add a conservation test: sum of all native balances + insurance fund + sum of unrealized PnL at mark is unchanged by a liquidation cycle.
ideas.reasoning: Force close (liquidation.rs:229-241) deletes the position and forgives whatever the trader cannot pay (balance clamped to 0, shortfall returned as remaining_deficit). auto_deleverage (L312-331) then reduces profitable counterparties' positions but credits them their FULL oracle-price PnL (`bal.available += realized_pnl`) and merely decrements the bookkeeping variable `loss_amount -= realized_pnl`; no balance anywhere is debited by the deficit. Positions are a zero-sum ledger (fill_transition credits realized PnL on close, position.rs:384-430, nobody is debited at that moment), so the winners' claims remain payable in full while the loser paid less than their loss: the system's total native balance grows by `remaining_deficit` per event. Under a volatile move (e.g. 10% gap on 20x positions, maintenance = notional/50 (margin.rs:216-225 with default tiers and 5000 bps)), a position's loss (10% of notional) exceeds its maintenance (2%) by 8% of notional — that 8% minus the trader's spare balance is minted for each liquidated account. The insurance fund is only ever credited (penalty, L214-218); socialize_loss is dead code from the executor's point of view. Also, ADL ranks by absolute unrealized PnL (L278), so one large profitable whale is closed first regardless of leverage — the opposite of the standard PnL%×leverage ranking, concentrating deleveraging on the largest, best-collateralised account.

ideas.title: Direct OutboundFailure on a live connection parks the consensus message until an unrelated reconnect
ideas.area: torus-network/swarm.rs direct send retry
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In the `TorusBehaviourEvent::Direct(OutboundFailure)` arm (crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:1601-1640): when `swarm.is_connected(&peer)` is true, re-send the tracked message immediately via `send_direct` (bounded attempts, e.g. 2, and skip if the message's view is already behind the pacemaker's current view) instead of only enqueueing into `pending_sends`. Keep the enqueue+dial path for the disconnected case. Optionally also drain `pending_sends[vk]` on every `Direct(Message::Response)` from that vk as a cheap safety net. Add a unit test in swarm.rs tests: connected dummy peer, inject `OutboundFailure::Timeout`, assert a second `send_request` is issued and `pending_sends` stays empty.
ideas.reasoning: The arm re-enqueues the tracked hotstuff message and calls `let _ = swarm.dial(peer)` (swarm.rs:1629-1638). `swarm.dial(PeerId)` builds `DialOpts::peer_id(p).build()` whose condition defaults to `PeerCondition::DisconnectedAndNotDialing` (libp2p-swarm-0.47.1 dial_opts.rs:90-98, 343-344), so for a peer that is still connected it returns `Err(DialPeerConditionFalse)` synchronously and does nothing. The only flush site for `pending_sends` is `SwarmEvent::ConnectionEstablished` (swarm.rs:2041). Therefore any failure that occurs while the QUIC connection stays up — `OutboundFailure::Timeout` (10 s request timeout, behaviour.rs:145), `Io("max sub-streams reached")` from the request-response worker cap, or an EOF when the receiver dropped the inbound stream — parks the vote / proposal / BlockDataResponse indefinitely. Failure scenario on the n=3 devnet (every vote required): leader L sends its proposal to V; V's swarm loop is stalled >10 s (the post-kill 60 s freeze, or a burst of inline pre-proposal batch decodes) so the ack never comes; L gets Timeout, parks the proposal, dial is a no-op; V never receives it; the view times out and every later view repeats until the L-V connection happens to drop and re-establish. When it finally does, a burst of stale parked messages (up to 256 per target, swarm.rs:3560) is replayed. Body-fetch responses travel on the same path (docs/perf/body-send-stages-diagnostic-2026-09-18.md), so a parked BlockDataResponse also strands the requester's fetch.

ideas.title: Every consensus unicast pays a full multistream-select RTT because `direct` advertises two protocols and the swarm uses V1, not V1Lazy
ideas.area: torus-network behaviour.rs / bridge.rs swarm config
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (1) In bridge.rs:312-314 add `.with_substream_upgrade_protocol_override(libp2p::core::upgrade::Version::V1Lazy)` to the swarm config. (2) Make the outbound protocol list for `direct` a single entry: after identify reports the peer's protocols, offer only `/torus/direct/2.0` (or drop `/1.0` outright once the fleet is on 2.0; `native_da`/`block_data` have the same 2-protocol shape). V1Lazy only elides the RTT when exactly one protocol is proposed, so both steps are required. (3) Longer term: keep one persistent per-peer bidi stream for hotstuff messages (libp2p-stream) so no per-message stream open/negotiate happens at all.
ideas.reasoning: Each `direct.send_request` opens a fresh QUIC bidi stream and negotiates the protocol with multistream-select. libp2p-swarm uses `upgrade::Version::default()` = `V1` unless overridden (connection.rs:557-573; multistream-select lib.rs:110-111), and the swarm config only sets the idle timeout (bridge.rs:312-314). In V1 the dialer flushes the proposal and awaits the listener's confirmation before writing the request (dialer_select.rs:136-150), i.e. 1 RTT before the first payload byte. Even with V1Lazy, the RTT is only skipped when `this.protocols.peek().is_none()`, and `direct` proposes both `/torus/direct/2.0` and `/1.0` (behaviour.rs:137-142). Per view the critical path is proposal (L->V) + vote (V->L'), each on a fresh stream: 1.5 RTT each instead of 0.5 RTT, so +2 RTT per view. Devnet loopback RTT ~0.05-0.1 ms: ~0 gain, which is why this has not shown up in the cells. Production WAN (config.rs:198,315 lists real public validator IPs): at 30 ms RTT the tax is 60 ms out of a ~620 ms view ≈ 10%; at 100 ms RTT it is 200 ms ≈ 30% of today's view length. Gossip mirrors proposals over gossipsub's persistent stream, so the proposal leg may partly bypass this, but votes are direct-only.

ideas.title: request-response worker cap (100/connection, inbound+outbound) is the real sub-stream limit; consensus shares it with 3.6 MB pushes and inbound overflow is a silent drop
ideas.area: torus-network behaviour.rs direct config / push routing
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (1) Route bulk traffic (pre-proposal pushes 0xFD, forward batches, BlockData bodies) through a dedicated request_response behaviour (e.g. `direct_bulk` with its own codec cap and `with_max_concurrent_streams(2*PUSH_MAX_INFLIGHT)`), leaving `direct` for hotstuff messages only; this gives consensus its own per-connection worker pool and its own FIFO `pending_outbound` queue, i.e. real prioritisation. (2) Set `request_response::Config::default().with_max_concurrent_streams(N)` explicitly for `direct` (behaviour.rs:145) with N sized from PUSH_MAX_INFLIGHT (32) x 2 directions + consensus headroom, and assert `N <= NATIVE_DA_STREAM_LIMIT` in the existing bridge.rs test so the QUIC window is provably not the binding limit. (3) Fix the `tune_quic_config` comment (bridge.rs:41-51): the 256->512 raise did not address the error it cites. (4) Expose a counter for the libp2p `Dropping inbound stream because we are at capacity` path (wrap the codec or watch for InboundFailure absence) so drops stop being invisible.
ideas.reasoning: `io::Error::other("max sub-streams reached")` exists only in libp2p-request-response handler.rs:199-209: it fires when `worker_streams.try_push` fails, and `worker_streams` is a `FuturesMap` bounded by `max_concurrent_streams` = 100 by default (lib.rs:316-319; handler.rs:113-115). The map holds inbound AND outbound futures for the connection, and each slot lives until the response is written: an outbound push holds its slot until the receiver's swarm loop decodes the batch and calls `send_response` (swarm.rs:1495-1520, 1575-1578); an inbound slot is held for the same turnaround. libp2p-quic's `max_concurrent_stream_limit` (256->512, bridge.rs:41-51) is never reached because request-response stops at 100 workers plus at most 128 negotiating inbound streams; the raise was applied to the wrong layer, and the 2,537x error count at bs=500 cited in that comment came from the worker cap. Concrete scenario: leader L has PUSH_MAX_INFLIGHT=32 pushes (~3.6 MB each pre-compression: 876.7 MB direct pre-bytes / ~120 val0 leads / 2 peers) outstanding to V; V is also receiving up to 32 pushes from the third validator plus forward batches, and its swarm loop is busy decoding them inline, so inbound slots stay occupied; when L's proposal or another validator's vote arrives on that connection, `try_push` fails and libp2p only logs `warn!("Dropping inbound stream because we are at capacity")` (handler.rs:163-168) with no InboundFailure event and no metric; the sender sees EOF on `read_response`, gets `OutboundFailure::Io`, and the message is parked by the bug in finding 1. In the s65-zerocode-push-r1 val1 log there are 0 such events (129 pushes sent, 287 received, 0 failures), so at cap 200 / 3 validators the budget is not exhausted; it becomes binding with larger batch sizes (bs=500 history) or more validators, and it is the only place where a 2 KB vote can be queued FIFO behind bulk in `pending_outbound` (handler.rs:446-452).

ideas.title: zstd-3 compress/decompress of the ~3.6 MB push envelope runs inside the libp2p connection task, once per peer, stalling that connection's consensus streams
ideas.area: torus-network codec.rs write_frame/read_frame
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In `write_length_prefixed_borsh_zstd` / `read_length_prefixed_borsh_zstd` (codec.rs:236-289), for frames above ~64 KB run `zstd::bulk::compress`/`decompress` under `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (or a small dedicated pool) and await it, so the connection task keeps polling the muxer. Better: compress the pre-proposal envelope once on the pre-proposal worker before `fan_native_push` (the envelope is already an `Arc<Vec<u8>>` shared across peers, swarm.rs:2504-2532) and add a `DirectPayload::PreCompressed` variant the codec writes verbatim, so the leader compresses 1x instead of once per validator.
ideas.reasoning: `write_request` for /2.0 calls `write_frame` -> `zstd::bulk::compress(&raw, 3)` synchronously inside the request-response worker future (codec.rs:264-276), which is polled by the connection's single task (libp2p-swarm connection/pool/task.rs:180-260; request-response handler.rs:390-400). While that future is computing, the task does not poll `connection.poll()`, so no new inbound stream is accepted and no other worker on that connection advances. Sizes from s65-zerocode-push-r1 val0: 876.7 MB pre-compression direct bytes over the run, ~120 val0 leads x 2 peers -> ~3.6 MB per push per peer, compressing 15.2x to ~240 KB on the wire. zstd-3 on that compressibility runs ~400-600 MB/s: ~6-9 ms of compress per peer connection per lead, plus ~1 ms for `try_to_vec` copying the 3.6 MB payload; the receiver pays ~2-3 ms decompress + a 3.6 MB allocation per push. The leader's proposal is sent right after the push on the same connection, so its stream negotiation and any inbound vote on that connection wait behind the compress: ~7-10 ms per view on the leader side, i.e. 1-1.5% of a 620 ms view, and the leader burns the compress CPU twice (once per peer). Small, but it is transport-level head-of-line blocking that a QUIC-level fix cannot remove.

ideas.title: Unbounded `method` label on torus_rpc_requests_total: any RPC client can grow node memory and blow up /metrics
ideas.area: torus-rpc / torus-telemetry (metrics cardinality, security)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs `MetricsLayer::call` (lines 405-430): stop using the raw client-supplied `request.method_name()` as a label value. Either (a) only label with names that are registered in the RpcModule (look up `inner`'s method set once at layer construction, map unknown names to a fixed `method="<unknown>"`), or (b) whitelist a small fixed set and bucket everything else as `other`. Additionally cap the label string length (e.g. 64 chars) as defence in depth, and consider `ServerConfig::max_request_body_size` smaller than jsonrpsee's 10 MiB default for the public RPC. Also make `torus_telemetry::serve_metrics` default bind `127.0.0.1:9090` instead of `0.0.0.0:9090` (crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:155) so the amplified scrape body is not publicly reachable.
ideas.reasoning: jsonrpsee 0.26 runs the RPC middleware BEFORE method lookup: the inner `RpcService::call` does `self.methods.method_with_name(&method)` and returns MethodNotFound (jsonrpsee-server-0.26.0/src/middleware/rpc.rs:89-92), so `MetricsLayer::call` sees every method string a client sends, including nonexistent ones, and always executes `m.rpc_requests_total.get_or_create(&vec![("method", method), ("status", status)]).inc()`. `Family<Vec<(String,String)>, Counter>` (prometheus-client 0.24.1 family.rs:104) is a HashMap that never evicts. The server config sets max_connections (64) and max_response_body_size only; `max_request_body_size` keeps jsonrpsee's TEN_MB default (server.rs:362), so one request may carry a ~10 MB unique method name that is then retained forever. Failure scenario: an unauthenticated client sends 10k req/s of `{"method":"x<random>"}` (a single RPC call is ~1 action today; val0 served 83,368 submits in one 300 s cell, so this rate is within the server's demonstrated capacity). At 1 KB per name that is ~10 MB/s of permanent growth (36 GB/h); at 1 MB names, 10k requests = 10 GB. Second effect: `/metrics` encode holds the Family read lock for the whole iteration (family.rs:418-420) while formatting one line per label set; with a 100 MB body, encode takes hundreds of ms, and parking_lot's writer-preferring RwLock makes every concurrent `get_or_create` (each RPC request takes read then write for a new key) queue behind it, so RPC latency spikes to encode time on every scrape. The bench sampler's `curl --max-time 3` (tools/matched-bench/sample_metrics.py:90) then marks scrapes invalid and Prometheus drops the target. Today's healthy cell shows the intended cardinality is 2 series (metrics-after-val0.txt: eth_blockNumber, torus_submitNativeActionsBin), so a fixed allowlist loses nothing.

ideas.title: serve_metrics accept loop dies permanently on the first accept() error (EMFILE/ECONNABORTED), silently losing /metrics for the process lifetime
ideas.area: torus-telemetry serve_metrics / torus-node wiring (observability liveness)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: crates/torus-telemetry/src/lib.rs:1949: replace `listener.accept().await?` inside the loop with a match that logs the error (rate-limited) and continues — on EMFILE/ENFILE sleep ~100 ms before retrying (the standard hyper/tokio pattern), on ECONNABORTED/ECONNRESET continue immediately. In crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:1019 keep the JoinHandle and log at error level if the task ever returns, so a dead telemetry endpoint is visible in the node log. Independently, set `set_max_open_files` on the RocksDB options in crates/torus-state/src/db.rs (currently unset, so RocksDB keeps every SST of all 44 CFs open) so the node does not drift toward fd exhaustion under archive mode.
ideas.reasoning: The accept loop is `loop { let (mut stream, _peer) = listener.accept().await?; ... }`: any accept error returns Err from the async fn, ending the spawned task; `tokio::spawn(serve_metrics(...))` at main.rs:1019 discards the JoinHandle so nothing logs it. Concrete scenario: the node holds fds for libp2p peer connections, up to 64 RPC connections, and every open SST across 44 column families (metrics-after-val0.txt shows 44 `{cf=...}` series; db.rs sets no max_open_files, so RocksDB's default of -1 = unlimited applies). When the process hits its RLIMIT_NOFILE, `accept4` returns EMFILE; from that moment `/metrics` is gone for the life of the process even after fds are freed, while consensus and RPC keep running. For the bench this means `scrape_one` at run-cell.sh:548 writes an empty metrics-after file, `mval torus_block_height` is empty, and the sampler logs scrape_valid=0 for the remainder of the cell — a whole 300 s cell lost with no node-side log line explaining why. In production Prometheus reports the target down while the node is fine, and the only recovery is a restart (which itself causes the ~60 s freeze noted in the measured state). Linux `accept` can also return ECONNABORTED for a connection reset between SYN and accept, which tokio surfaces as Err; this is a transient condition that should never kill the listener.

ideas.title: RocksDB statistics tickers are ON by default since r3 (deviates from the 'exact-today' baseline) with no A/B cell measuring the cost
ideas.area: torus-state DB tuning / bench validity (metrics collection inside the hot path)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Run one matched-bench A/B pair with `EXTRA_ENV='TORUS_ROCKSDB_STATS=0'` vs the default (level 1) at cap 200, same 300 s cell, and record the delta in docs/perf. If the delta is within noise, document that and keep tickers on; if not, flip the default in crates/torus-state/src/db.rs `parse_rocksdb_stats_level` (`None => 1` → `None => 0`) and have the bench harness opt in explicitly (it already passes EXTRA_ENV through; the 29 torus_rocksdb_* gauges simply read 0 when stats are off, which run-cell.sh already tolerates).
ideas.reasoning: db.rs:40-48 says every DbTuning default is 'EXACT-TODAY except stats_level (tickers on…)', and db.rs:217-222 enables `opts.enable_statistics()` at `StatsLevel::ExceptHistogramOrTimers` whenever TORUS_ROCKSDB_STATS is unset (parse_rocksdb_stats_level: `None => 1`). That means every RocksDB Get/Put/WriteBatch on the exec thread, the flush worker, and compaction threads now executes `RecordTick` (core-local relaxed atomics) for every ticker RocksDB fires, and this is the production default, not a bench-only knob. No doc in docs/perf shows a `TORUS_ROCKSDB_STATS=0` cell (grep finds only the =2 attribution run), so the cost of the instrumentation has never been separated from the numbers it was added to explain. Arithmetic for the expected size: tickers at this level are ~5-10 relaxed atomic adds per Get (memtable hit/miss, block-cache hit/miss, bytes read, keys read) ≈ 20-50 ns; at O(100k) state reads/s on the exec thread that is ~2-5 ms/s ≈ 0.2-0.5% of one core, and writes are batched so per-key cost is smaller. With the hotstuff thread ~70% idle and storage measured as not the blocker, the effect on matched/s is most likely 0-1% — small, but it is the only place where metrics collection sits inside the execution hot path, and the deviation from the exact-today baseline should be either measured or reverted rather than assumed.

ideas.title: Header/body consistency, action cap and pipelined parent-hash are enforced only as exec-time FATAL fail-stops; validate_block never rejects them and no test says it should
ideas.area: torus-consensus/app.rs validate path (validate_datum_after_fail_stop, validate_body_checks_core, finish_validate)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs `validate_datum_after_fail_stop` (L4389) add deterministic structural checks BEFORE `validate_body_checks_core`: (a) `native_actions.len() == header.native_action_count as usize` and `evm_transactions.len() == header.evm_tx_count as usize`; (b) `native_actions.len() <= torus_mempool::rate_limit::native_total_block_cap()`, order count <= `native_orders_per_block_cap()`, encoded bytes <= `native_block_bytes_cap()`; (c) on the CompactBlock branch of `decode_proposal_and_ensure_durable_core` (L4224) compare `native_action_hashes.len()` to `header.native_action_count` before any DA reconstruction, so a bad block costs no DA read. Add unit tests next to `validate_block_legacy_durable` (L8317): count-mismatch datum -> `Invalid`; over-cap datum -> `Invalid`; and a pipelined case (self.last_header two heights behind, wrong parent_hash) documenting today's `Valid` verdict so the deferral is a conscious choice. All three rules are pure functions of the datum bytes, so heterogeneous deployment cannot fork on them — but they ARE consensus-validity changes and must ship to all validators together (same caveat the code already states at L4477-4483 for the session fix).
ideas.reasoning: Today's vote-time checks are: datums.len()==1 (L4756), sha256 binding (L4394), EVM decode + native signature/attestation (L4466-4531), and an ancestry check that runs ONLY when `self.last_header.height + 1 == height` (L4552) — the code itself says it DEFERS otherwise. With header-first pipelining (measured ~1.5 views per committed block) the parent is usually still pending at vote time, so the ancestry check is skipped for most proposals and the exec-time `detect_parent_link_violation` (L1465) is the real guard. Likewise `native_actions.len() != header.native_action_count` is checked only at L1412 in `execute_committed_block_with`, where it latches `exec_failed`. The block-size caps are applied only in `select_block_payload` (L5118-5140); its own comment says 'validate_block rejects on neither action nor order count'. Failure scenario: one leader — buggy (e.g. a refactor of `mirror_or_drop_native` L4600 leaving `native_action_count` stale) or Byzantine — proposes a CompactBlock whose header count differs from its hash list. All honest validators vote (nothing compares them), the block commits under a QC, then EVERY validator's exec thread hits L1412 and latches. Once latched, produce_block (L4592), validate_block (L4747) and on_committed_block (L4811) all refuse, so the chain halts on all nodes; a restart replays the committed height via `replay_committed` -> `execute_committed_block` (L3624-3656) and latches again. Net: a single faulty node converts into a permanent whole-chain halt needing manual DB surgery, i.e. zero fault tolerance for this class. The existing tests (`execute_partial_body_vs_header_count_fail_stops` L11310, `parent_link_violation_rejects_mismatched_parent` L6739) only prove the LATCH fires; none proves the vote is withheld. The bench cannot surface this because its leaders are all honest and identical.

ideas.title: Block header timestamp is proposer-chosen wall clock and never validated at vote time, yet it is the consensus input to session-key expiry and to persisted trade/order timestamps
ideas.area: torus-consensus app.rs produce_block/finish_validate; torus-types eip712 session verification
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In `finish_validate` (app.rs:4536) add: (1) deterministic lower bound — when `self.last_header` is the parent, reject if `header.timestamp < self.last_header.timestamp` (monotone, same deferral rule as the ancestry check when the parent is pending); (2) local-clock upper bound — reject if `header.timestamp > now + MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_SECS` (e.g. 15 s, the usual Ethereum/Tendermint drift allowance). Add unit tests beside `validate_block_legacy_durable` (L8317): ts = parent.ts - 1 -> Invalid; ts = now + 3600 -> Invalid; ts within bounds -> Valid. Longer term, also enforce the lower bound at exec via `detect_parent_link_violation`-style check so a pipelined block cannot slip a regression past the deferred vote check.
ideas.reasoning: produce_block sets `timestamp = SystemTime::now()` (app.rs:4633-4636) and no code in the validate path examines it: the only `timestamp` uses below L5100 are as INPUT to `batch_verify_native_actions` (L4494 non-attested validate, L1649/L1826/L1839 exec). eip712.rs:1143 accepts a session-signed action only if `timestamp <= session.expiry`, so the leader's clock decides which session actions are valid. Trade and maker records serialise the block timestamp (native_executor.rs:269,282) and orders carry it (order_book.rs:45,60,371). Concrete failure: a leader whose clock is +1 h (NTP step, VM resume) proposes attested blocks that all validators vote for; at exec every session-signed action fails the expiry check and is dropped without slash (this drop semantics is what `missing_session_at_exec_drops_action_no_slash` L9668 pins). At n=3 that leader owns ~1/3 of views, so roughly a third of the DEX's session-key order flow silently disappears from the chain — no fork, no vote failure, no error at ingress, only fills/s falling. A leader with a backwards clock resurrects expired sessions (auth bypass) and writes non-monotone timestamps into trade history. Every bench cell runs 3 validators on ONE host with one clock, so this class is structurally invisible to the current evidence; no test in the app.rs inventory (L5682-12621) touches timestamp bounds.

Items deliberately NOT reported because they are excluded angles or already covered: pacemaker timeout/TC formation tests (timeouts excluded), leader-reputation code in hotstuff/types.rs (leader rotation excluded), torus-bridge/src/validator.rs BlockValidator having no direct unit tests (it is the EVM re-execution path, exercised via bridge_tests.rs:140-152 and app.rs). One adjacent observation folded into finding 1 rather than listed separately: on the non-attested path (sig_attestation == [0;64]) `header.proposer` is never checked against the validator set or the view leader while it is the fee beneficiary (validator.rs:146,248,409; native_executor.rs:5815); worth a test if fee_validator_bps is ever non-zero. No cargo commands, no greps over target/, no file writes, no memory writes were performed.

ideas.title: --restore-from-snapshot has no producer: SnapshotManager is dead code, so a pruned network has no bootstrap path
ideas.area: torus-state/snapshot.rs, torus-node/main.rs, torus-consensus exec pipeline
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Wire a producer for the existing snapshot machinery. Option A (in-process): construct `SnapshotManager` in torus-node from a `--snapshot-interval/--snapshot-dir` flag and call `create_and_prune` from the exec thread right after a block's flush batch lands (the per-block batch already carries state + META_NATIVE_APPLIED_HEIGHT atomically, app.rs comments around 1595-1605, so a checkpoint at that instant is a consistent applied-height image). Fill `SnapshotMetadata.state_root` from the CF_BLOCK_HEADERS record at that height (TorusBlockHeader.state_root, torus-types/src/lib.rs:401), not from a recompute. Option B (out-of-process, S effort): a `torus-node snapshot --data-dir` subcommand next to crates/torus-node/src/bin/ that opens the DB read-only, reads META_NATIVE_APPLIED_HEIGHT, and calls `StateDb::create_snapshot`. Either way, add an integration test that boots a fresh node from the produced snapshot and block-syncs to the tip.
ideas.reasoning: snapshot.rs:224-292 defines SnapshotManager::should_snapshot/create_and_prune, and lib.rs:32 re-exports it, but the code graph shows create_snapshot's only callers are create_and_prune and the module's own tests, and create_and_prune is only called from tests. main.rs:469-477 implements the consumer (`--restore-from-snapshot`) and three docs advertise it to operators (configuration-reference.md:33 'must have been created by the node's snapshot system'; pruning-guide.md:154-164 'if you have a snapshot from an archive node'; node-operator-guide.md:108-109), yet no binary can create one. Failure scenario: every validator runs `--retention-blocks N` (the documented validator mode, pruning-guide.md:141). The block-tree pruner deletes BLOCK_AT_HEIGHT below the horizon (internal.rs:1880-1890). A new validator starts at genesis and asks any peer for height 0: `blocks_from_height_to_newest` (public.rs:46-82) finds no block_at_height(0), exits the while loop with an empty prefix, then appends the SPECULATIVE tail blocks whose parents the client does not have; insert/app_view fails, blocks_synced stays 0, `end_session` bumps consecutive_futile_sessions and the trigger backs off to 8x60 s = 480 s (client.rs:927-935, 1141-1143). The node never joins and never says why. The pruning guide's only recovery ('re-sync from an archive peer') requires an archive node that the guide itself says is optional.

ideas.title: Snapshot restore rolls back hotstuff vote state (cf_consensus_meta is copied verbatim), undoing the f05b20e vote-persistence guarantee
ideas.area: torus-state/snapshot.rs restore_from_snapshot, torus-consensus/kv_store.rs, hotstuff_rs block_tree variables
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In `restore_from_snapshot` (snapshot.rs:161-217), treat cf_consensus_meta specially: (1) if a local data_dir exists, open both DBs and carry forward the LOCAL values of the vote-safety keys (HIGHEST_VIEW_PHASE_VOTED, LAST_VOTED_PROPOSAL, HIGHEST_VIEW_ENTERED, LOCKED_PC, HIGHEST_PC, plus the timeout-vote equivalents) when they are higher/newer than the snapshot's, or refuse the restore if the local highest-voted view exceeds the snapshot's and no `--i-know-what-i-am-doing` flag is set; (2) when the snapshot came from another validator, clear the producer's per-key vote variables and speculative/leader-reputation entries so the importing node starts with vote state = 'never voted after view H'. Add a test that restores an older self-snapshot and asserts HIGHEST_VIEW_PHASE_VOTED did not decrease.
ideas.reasoning: create_snapshot uses RocksDB Checkpoint over the whole DB (snapshot.rs:87-91); ALL_CF_NAMES (cf.rs:161-206) includes CF_CONSENSUS_META, and kv_store.rs:1-14 states that ALL block-tree state, including HIGHEST_VIEW_PHASE_VOTED, lives in that CF. restore_from_snapshot copies the directory and swaps it in (snapshot.rs:184-209) with no special handling. Concrete scenario: validator V votes in view v for block B (persisted before send since f05b20e), crashes, operator restores V's own periodic snapshot taken at view v-k. V restarts with highest_view_voted = v-k and highest_view_entered rolled back too. Any leader that re-broadcasts (or a Byzantine leader that crafts) a view-v proposal for B' != B now passes V's 'already voted in this view' check, and V signs a second vote in view v. At n=3 the quorum is all 3 so the duplicate can form a conflicting QC only with collusion, but at n>=4 with f Byzantine nodes an honest-but-restored validator's double vote is exactly the extra vote needed for two conflicting QCs, and it is slashable equivocation regardless. The same copy also imports the PRODUCER's vote variables when the snapshot is transferred between validators (the intended use per pruning-guide.md:156 'a snapshot from an archive node').

ideas.title: AdvertiseBlock carries no 'lowest available height', so a syncing node keeps picking peers that already pruned the range it needs
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs block_sync messages.rs/server.rs/client.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Add `lowest_available_height` (= block_tree_pruned_height or 0) to AdvertiseBlock (messages.rs:121-126; it is inside the signed tuple so bump the wire version) and to the server's advertisement (server.rs:170-186). In the client, extend `register_or_update_sync_server` to store (lowest, highest) and make `random_sync_server` filter peers by `lowest <= start_height` as well as the existing `highest >= peer_min_height` (client.rs:728-742). In the server, when `start_height < pruned_floor` respond with an explicit empty BlockSyncResponse instead of the speculative tail (public.rs:74-82) so the client's worker returns `Empty` immediately rather than waiting 3 s for a timeout (main.rs:806). When no peer covers start_height, log one explicit 'need archive peer or snapshot from height >= X' line instead of the generic 'no available sync servers'.
ideas.reasoning: Today `random_sync_server` only knows each peer's highest committed height (client.rs:591-608, messages.rs:121-126). A node behind by more than a peer's retention window (or bootstrapping from genesis) selects a pruned peer, whose server returns an empty committed prefix plus the speculative tail; the client cannot insert those (unknown parents), the session ends futile, backoff climbs to 480 s (client.rs:1141-1143), and if a fetch times out instead the honest peer is even blacklisted for the shortfall (client.rs:902-924, 10 s expiry). With n=3 there are only two candidate servers, so one archive peer among pruned ones is found only by luck of `IteratorRandom::choose`. Arithmetic: with 1 archive peer of 2 candidates, expected sessions to hit it is 2, each futile miss costing 60 s x 2^k (k = consecutive futile) plus the 30 s session cap -- typically 1.5-8 min of dead time per rejoin, and unbounded when no archive peer exists.

ideas.title: Replay-based catch-up is exec-bound at ~0.58 s per native block (barely faster than production); a checkpoint-transfer design cuts join time by >95%
ideas.area: torus-consensus app.rs sync path, torus-state snapshot.rs, torus-network (new request-response protocol)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Build snapshot transfer on top of the existing checkpoint code: (1) producer from finding 1 at a fixed interval (e.g. every 5,000 blocks, keep 2); (2) a libp2p request-response protocol `/torus/snapshot/1.0` with `Manifest{height, block_hash, state_root, files:[(name,len,blake3)]}` and `GetChunk{file, offset, len}` (or serve the checkpoint dir over the existing RPC HTTP port); (3) client flow in torus-node: if `--sync-from-snapshot` and local DB is empty, fetch the manifest from a validator, fetch the QC-certified header at `height` via the existing block-sync response (BlockSyncResponse.highest_pc + header), require `manifest.state_root == header.state_root` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:401) -- NOT the self-attested `snapshot_metadata.json` that verify_snapshot trusts today (snapshot.rs:112-116, 140-160) -- download files, run `verify_snapshot`, `restore_from_snapshot` (with the cf_consensus_meta handling from finding 2), then let the normal block-sync client continue from highest_committed+1 (compute_sync_start, client.rs:655-702, already does this). Measure `verify_snapshot` cost first: it recomputes the EVM root and the full native root by scanning the whole DB (snapshot.rs:132-140).
ideas.reasoning: Catch-up throughput is bounded by the execution pipeline, not by the network: in cell s65-votefix-fix270-r3, torus_exec_block_seconds_sum = 278.9 s over 473 native blocks (1,559 executions total, the ~1,086 empty ones cost microseconds), i.e. ~0.58 s per native block; the exec thread was 83.4% busy at 711.8 ms per native block in the load window. Maximum replay rate is therefore ~1.7 native blocks/s. Against a production rate of 1.1-1.6 native blocks/s (task brief: ~1.1/s; the cell committed 473 native blocks in 300 s = 1.58/s), a lagging node gains only 0.1-0.6 blocks/s on the tip: replaying one hour of full-load chain takes 0.58 x 3600 x 1.1 = 38 min to 0.58 x 3600 x 1.58 = 55 min, and a node that missed 10 min of full load needs 10 x 1.58 / 0.14 = ~110 min to actually reach the tip at 1.58 blocks/s production (~20 min at 1.1/s). The sync path additionally pulls bodies inline on the hotstuff-algo thread per block (validate_block_for_sync -> pull_compact_bodies_if_missing, app.rs:4775-4801; 1-8 s budget via sync_pull_retries, app.rs:2582-2591) and blocks on the 64-deep exec queue (rate_limit.rs:299) once it runs ahead. A checkpoint transfer replaces replay with a file copy: the checkpoint is hardlink-instant (snapshot.rs:87-91); the cell wrote flush_write_bytes = 2.0 GB of SSTs during ~300 s of full load (torus_rocksdb_flush_write_bytes, before compaction), so an hour of full-load chain is on the order of a few GB post-compaction, i.e. tens of seconds on a 1 Gbit LAN versus 38-55 min of replay: >95% reduction for any join that is >= 1 h behind, and replay cost stops scaling with chain age. This matters at n>=4 (where the chain keeps moving while a validator is down) and for RPC/explorer nodes; at n=3 the chain freezes during downtime so the gap is small.

ideas.title: Consensus-visible env knobs (TORUS_BOOK_ROWS) fork silently: CTE headers carry no execution root and validate_block never compares state
ideas.area: torus-consensus app.rs / torus-bridge native_executor.rs / state_root.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Put an execution commitment back on chain: have produce_block write a LAGGED exec root (native+EVM root of the newest height the exec pipeline has finished, e.g. H-k with k = exec queue depth) into the header, and have validate_block (app.rs:4737) refuse to vote when its own executed root for that height differs. Lagged means it never blocks the CTE hot path. 2) Cheaper interim: add a 'state-format fingerprint' (book_mode.marker_byte(), level-hash chunked flag, native-root scheme version) to the hotstuff genesis app_state written in main.rs:497-499 (Genesis::to_hotstuff_genesis) and to every proposal; validate_block rejects proposals whose fingerprint differs from the local one, and the __book_mode__ marker (native_executor.rs:2445-2460) is written AT GENESIS INIT rather than on first save. 3) Fix the stale comment in crates/torus-bridge/src/state_root.rs:23 ('the validator StateRootMismatch check remains the live safety net') — on this branch there is no such check.
ideas.reasoning: Regime: produce_block sets header.state_root = parent_header.state_root (app.rs:4580 comment, app.rs:4675) so it is 0x0 forever; agreement.jsonl in cell s65-zerocode-r270-r3 shows header_state_root=0x000..0 at height 1180 and run-cell.sh:562-563 states 'the header stateRoot is 0x0 on this branch; the digest is the ONLY determinism check'. validate_block (app.rs:4737-4766) checks only datums.len()==1 and datum hash/sigs/DA durability, never executed state. Meanwhile native_executor.rs:579-590 says TORUS_BOOK_ROWS changes the state-root FORMAT ('a mixed fleet forks at the first block that touches any book'). The only guard is the node-local __book_mode__ marker, which is written on FIRST SAVE (native_executor.rs:2447) and checked at boot (1833-1851) — so it catches a wrong-flag RESTART but not a fresh fleet where one node was launched with a different value: at genesis all markers are absent, every node writes its own marker, all three vote normally, and the books CF (one of the 6 native-root CFs) diverges silently from the first native block. Nothing on chain or in consensus ever notices; the fork surfaces only when a harness runs the post-hoc state_digest RPC scan or when clients see different fills on different RPC nodes. Concrete scenario today: tools/matched-bench/run-cell.sh:167 exports TORUS_BOOK_ROWS=3 for its nodes, while devnet/docker-compose.yml (env at :32-39) and devnet/wsl/env.sh set no TORUS_BOOK_ROWS (Classic). A validator restarted via launch-3val.sh outside run-cell, or a 4th node joined from the compose profile, joins a mode-3 chain cleanly (marker absent on its fresh DB), votes on every block, and holds a different order-book state — a 2-vs-1 or 1-vs-1-vs-1 native-state fork with n=3 still producing QCs. The same class applies to any future knob that changes persisted root-CF bytes.

ideas.title: genesis.json is re-read on every boot and never pinned to the DB: an edited genesis on one validator silently changes its leader schedule, timeouts, and fee routing
ideas.area: torus-node main.rs / torus-genesis / torus-types ChainConfig
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: On first init (main.rs:491-500) persist keccak(genesis file bytes) and the resolved ChainConfig (bincode) into a node-local CF next to the __book_mode__/__next_global_order_id__ rows. On every later boot recompute and compare; on mismatch fail-stop with a diff of the changed fields unless `--accept-genesis-change` is passed. Additionally include the genesis hash in the hotstuff genesis app_state (Genesis::to_hotstuff_genesis, torus-genesis lib.rs:557) so a node initialised from a different genesis cannot form or join a QC at all. Log the genesis hash at boot next to the existing chain_id/epoch_length info line (main.rs:512-514).
ideas.reasoning: main.rs:485-507: `chain_config` is always taken from the genesis file passed on the CLI/config; only the state seeding is skipped when the DB is non-empty ('database already initialized, skipping genesis'). No genesis hash is stored anywhere (no genesis_hash/fingerprint symbol in torus-genesis or torus-state). Fields that flow from the file into live behaviour on EVERY boot: reputation_leader_selection (main.rs:753-755; the code itself says 'every validator must run the same setting or replicas disagree on leaders and finalization halts'), timeout_base_ms / backoff_factor / backoff_cap / commit_lag_backoff_cap (main.rs:797-802, pacemaker deadline schedule), epoch_length (main.rs:798), and treasury_address / dev_pool_address / fee bps (genesis lib.rs:492-525 -> TorusApp treasury_address app.rs:503, :3212-3221 -> native fee settlement, i.e. root-CF state). Failure scenario A (liveness): an operator regenerates devnet/wsl/genesis-3val.json with reputation_leader_selection=true (or a different timeout_base_ms) and restarts only val1: val1 computes a different leader for view v, rejects/ignores val0's proposal, n=3 needs all 3 votes -> every view times out; the log shows nothing except 'database already initialized, skipping genesis'. Failure scenario B (safety): the same restart with a changed treasury_address or fee split: val1 credits fees to a different account -> root-CF divergence, undetectable per the previous finding. Multi-box deployments (docker-compose mounts ./genesis.json:ro per container, devnet/docker-compose.yml:41) make per-node genesis revisions a realistic ops mistake.

ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Add a single `consensus_fingerprint()` in torus-node that hashes the resolved values of the knobs the code itself marks fleet-uniform or consensus-visible: TORUS_BOOK_ROWS (native_executor.rs:656), TORUS_COMMIT_LAG_BACKOFF_CAP resolution (main.rs:333), reputation_leader_selection, timeout_base_ms/backoff_*, epoch_length, chain_id, genesis hash (finding 2), plus the marker bytes. (a) Log it once at boot with every input value; (b) expose it as a metric `torus_consensus_fingerprint_info{fingerprint="<hex>"} 1` so run-cell.sh can compare /metrics across nodes instead of md5-ing /proc/<pid>/environ (run-cell.sh:391-393, which only works for same-host fleets and only logs 'must be a single value' without aborting); (c) put the fingerprint into the libp2p identify agent_version (currently the constant "/torus/1.0", behaviour.rs:210) and log ERROR + a `torus_peer_fingerprint_mismatch_total` counter when a registered validator advertises a different one. (d) Make run-cell.sh die when ENV_VERIFY has more than one digest.
ideas.reasoning: There are 70 std::env::var read sites across the workspace (grep count), each in its own OnceLock/fresh-read helper; nothing enumerates them, nothing logs the full resolved set, and peers exchange no configuration at all. The bench harness compensates for the same-host case (run-cell.sh:376-393: clears TORUS_*, exports RECORD_ENV, then md5s each node's environ) but merely logs the digests; a mismatch during a 300 s cell would produce a 'clean' summary until the post-hoc digest step. With (a)-(c) a mis-set validator is visible in its own log within 1 s of boot and in every peer's log at identify time, before the first native block. Arithmetic on cost: one keccak of ~200 bytes at boot plus one string in identify — zero steady-state cost.

ideas.title: Zero-margin, uncapped stop orders turn every fill into an O(S) scan of pending_stops (matching-engine DoS)
ideas.area: torus-core order_book.rs (place_order / trigger_stops), torus-bridge native_executor.rs (Phase 2 reserve, stop-row save)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Count pending stops toward MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET (order_book.rs:410 only counts `trader_orders`, i.e. resting orders) or add a separate per-trader stop cap. 2) Reserve margin for stop orders at placement: reserve_for_qty is called with `params.price`, which is ZERO for stops (order_book.rs:3060/3092 tests, native_executor.rs:4765-4771 and 3629-3635) so `reserve_for_qty_cfg` returns ZERO (4659) and the balance check is skipped; reserve on `limit` (StopLimit) or trigger×qty (StopMarket). 3) Reject triggers outside a band around last_trade_price (today a Buy stop with an astronomically high trigger is accepted and never fires). 4) Re-index `pending_stops` as two BTreeMaps keyed by trigger price (buy stops ascending, sell stops descending) so `trigger_stops` pops only fired entries (O(log S + fired)) instead of `Vec::retain` over all S (order_book.rs:1284-1296); likewise `cancel_all`'s `pending_stops.retain` (651, 695).
ideas.reasoning: Every place_order that produces at least one fill calls trigger_stops (order_book.rs:577-579), which runs `self.pending_stops.retain(..)` over the whole Vec (1284). Stops are pushed unbounded (438, 474): the per-trader cap counts resting orders only, and the only validation is dust qty >= lot (377) and trigger direction (424-437). With price ZERO the executor reserves nothing and never reads the balance, so an unfunded address can place them; ingress validates only market existence (torus.rs:250-274). Arithmetic on cell s65-zerocode-r270-r3: fills_per_native_block 50,047 across 10 markets = ~5k fill-producing place_order calls per market per block. StopOrder is ~130 B, so S = 10k stops in one market = 1.3 MB scanned per call, ~0.1-0.15 ms memory-bound; 5k calls x 0.13 ms = ~0.6 s of extra Phase-3 time per block for that market, vs the current engine cost of ~8 ms/1k fills x 50 = ~0.4 s/block (summary.json engine_ms_per_1k_fills 7.97). Phase 3 is per-market serial on the critical path, so matched/s falls by >50%; 100k stops (allowed: orders cap 100k per block, batch cap 1024) makes it ~6 s/block. Attacker cost: 10k stops = 10 PlaceOrderBatch actions from one address, zero balance, zero fees (native fees are never charged: total_native_fees only initialised at 1880 and read at 5805). Secondary: every save re-encodes all S stops (`stop_rows`, order_book.rs:1375-1390) and prefix-scans all persisted stop rows (`diff_stop_rows`, native_executor.rs:2898-2936) per dirty market per block.

ideas.title: Fills produced by triggered stop orders are dropped from settlement: free liquidity wipe and stranded maker margin
ideas.area: torus-core order_book.rs trigger_stops; torus-bridge native_executor.rs exec_place_order / Phase 4 settlement; market_workers.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Make trigger_stops return (or accumulate on the book, e.g. `triggered_results: Vec<(Address, PlaceResult)>`) every PlaceResult it generates, and have the executor drain and settle them exactly like prepared-order results: apply_fill for taker and maker, maker_margin_releases for consumed/STP-cancelled makers, persist_trade, and release/charge the stop owner's margin (which needs finding 1's reserve at placement). Until then, disable stop order types at ingress (validate_known_markets-style reject) so the book cannot be swept without settlement.
ideas.reasoning: trigger_stops converts a fired stop into a Market/Limit order and calls `self.place_order` (order_book.rs:1302-1316) but only inspects `result.status` for a warn (1317-1327); the fills and self_trade_cancels are discarded. The executor settles only the outer PlaceResult: exec_place_order iterates `result.fills` of the order it placed (native_executor.rs:4871-4905) and Phase 4 iterates the MatchResult.result of each prepared order (market_workers.rs:313-321). Maker orders consumed by the triggered order are already popped from the queue (match_at_level 1129-1136), so: makers lose their resting orders, receive no position, their reservation stays in order_margin forever (maker_margin_releases only covers fills in `results`, 4684-4750), no trade rows are written, and last_trade_price moves. Failure scenario: attacker places a StopMarket sell, qty = total bid depth, trigger one tick below last price, price ZERO (zero margin, no balance needed, finding 1); the next down-tick fires it as a market order (is_market=true in place_order, 507) that sweeps the whole bid side; the bids vanish with no economic transfer to anyone. Cost: one signature. Repeatable every block on every market; a market maker's entire quoted depth is deleted while its margin stays locked.
