crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4871-4905 (settles only result.fills of the outer order), 4684-4750 (maker releases derived from the batch's results only)
crates/torus-bridge/src/market_workers.rs:313-321 (worker returns one PlaceResult per prepared request)
memory 9dc45e44cd8c20e6: the earlier fix was 'observability only', fills remained discarded
ideas.expected_improvement: prevents zero-cost deletion of resting liquidity and permanent maker-margin stranding; restores conservation of margin (total released == total reserved) when stops fire
ideas.risk: Settling triggered fills changes state roots for any block in which a stop fires (lockstep deploy); needs a deterministic ordering rule for triggered results relative to prepared results in Phase 4.
ideas.why_new: Not in docs/perf/s64-exploration-2026-09-24.md; memory search returned only the HIGH-NEW-08 log-only fix.

ideas.title: Triggered stop orders allocate an order id that collides with the next pre-assigned batch id (state divergence / boot fail-stop)
ideas.area: torus-bridge market_workers.rs match_market; native_executor.rs Phase 2 id assignment; torus-core order_book.rs alloc_id
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Stop using the book's `alloc_id` for triggered orders inside a batch. Options: (a) execute triggered stops in a post-batch pass with fresh ids taken from ctx.next_global_order_id after all prepared orders (also what finding 2 needs for settlement); (b) give each MatchRequest a reserved id gap or per-market high-water so `set_next_order_id(req.order_id)` can never reset below an id already handed out; (c) at minimum, debug_assert in insert_order that `order_index` did not already contain the id, and reject batches that would trigger a resting stop until fixed.
ideas.reasoning: Phase 2 assigns contiguous ids: each passing prepared order takes `ctx.next_global_order_id` and increments by 1 (native_executor.rs:~3590-3600 and the serial loop). In the worker, `book.set_next_order_id(req.order_id)` precedes every place_order (market_workers.rs:313-315). If that order's fills fire a StopLimit that rests, trigger_stops' inner place_order calls alloc_id (order_book.rs:356-360, 373) and hands out req.order_id + 1, which is exactly the id already assigned to the next prepared order (same or another market). The post-batch high-water update (native_executor.rs:3975-3977, 4340-4342) cannot undo it. Two live orders then share one id: in the same book, order_index/order_seq entries are overwritten (1197, 1202) and the row store persists a single row per id (row_journal keyed by id, encode_order_row via order_index), so a node that restarts rebuilds a different book than the resident nodes and the boot verify of recomputed level rows fail-stops (native_executor.rs:~576 comment) or, in classic mode, produces a different level/state root; across books, exec_cancel_order finds the first Ok while iterating `ctx.order_books` (a HashMap, 4978/4991), so which order gets cancelled differs per process: a consensus fork. Attacker-triggerable at zero cost via finding 1 (zero-margin StopLimit with a resting limit price).
evidence: crates/torus-bridge/src/market_workers.rs:313-329 (set_next_order_id per request, next_order_id read once at the end)
crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:356-360 alloc_id, 373 (place_order allocates), 1302-1316 (trigger_stops re-enters place_order), 1197/1202 (HashMap inserts overwrite)
crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3975-3977, 4340-4342 (high-water only raises), 4978-4991 (HashMap iteration in exec_cancel_order)
ideas.expected_improvement: prevents duplicate order ids (non-deterministic cancels, lost rows, restart fail-stop / fork) whenever a stop fires inside a batch
ideas.risk: I traced the path in code but did not execute a reproduction (read-only round); a unit test placing a batch [limit that fills, StopLimit trigger] followed by another prepared order should confirm the duplicate id.
ideas.why_new: No prior finding in s64 doc or memory mentions triggered-stop id allocation within the pre-assigned-id batch pipeline.

ideas.title: Junk CancelOrder actions are free, validated nowhere, and take the cancels-first prefix of every block (block-slot starvation)
ideas.area: torus-rpc torus.rs admission; torus-mempool native_pool.rs SortKey/eviction/selection; torus-bridge exec_cancel_order
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Ingress screen (node-local, cannot fork): reject CancelOrder whose order_id >= the RPC node's next_global_order_id or whose id is absent from the resident book's order_index / not owned by the sender (one HashMap lookup; add a read-only accessor from the exec context or a shared snapshot). 2) Cap the cancels-first prefix per block (e.g. min(pending cancels, 25% of NATIVE_TOTAL_BLOCK_CAP) unless no non-cancels are pooled) in select_for_block_with_senders_excluding and the cancels-only pacing tier. 3) Count failed cancels per sender at exec and feed a per-sender ingress penalty, or charge a minimal native fee for any action (total_native_fees is never incremented today).
ideas.reasoning: A CancelOrder with a random id passes ingress: validate_known_markets returns Ok for non-place actions (torus.rs:271), verify_one_action checks only signature/nonce/session (284-305); the pool dedups only identical hashes (native_pool.rs:186) and the nonce is a client timestamp within +/-60 s, so unlimited distinct cancels per address. Cancels bypass the s65 admission shed (torus.rs:1119-1128, 436-437), evict a non-cancel when the pool is full (native_pool.rs:199-207), and sort first in every selection (SortKey priority byte 0, 217; 336-385) and exclusively in the cancels-only pacing tier (395-412). At exec they cost the sender nothing: exec_cancel_order scans the books and returns err (4972-5017) with no fee or balance effect. Arithmetic: block cap 200 actions, per-sender-per-block 64, per-sender pool 512 (rate_limit.rs:29, 41, 84): 4 addresses x 64 = 256 >= 200, so four keys sending 200 x 1.1 blocks/s = 220 signed cancels/s fill every block with junk; honest PlaceOrderBatch actions are never selected and matched/s goes to ~0 while the flood lasts (the bench already sustains 343 actions/s from one host). 128 addresses x 512 = 65,536 cancels also evict every pooled order (NATIVE_POOL_MAX_SIZE 65,536, rate_limit.rs:53). Junk cancels also cost each validator the ECDSA verify, a DA mirror write and gossip.

crates/torus-mempool/src/native_pool.rs:13-25 and 217 (cancels sort first), 186 (dedup by hash only), 199-207 (cancel evicts non-cancel), 336-385 and 395-412 (selection)
crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4972-5017 (failed cancel: no charge), 1457/1880/5805 (total_native_fees never incremented)
crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:29, 41, 53, 84 (per-block 64, block cap 200, pool 65,536, per-sender 512)
ideas.expected_improvement: prevents a zero-cost attack that drops matched/s to ~0 for the duration of the flood; the cancel-prefix cap alone bounds the loss to the cap fraction (e.g. 25%)
ideas.risk: An existence check at ingress needs a consistent read of the resident book (the RPC node may lag the leader by a block, so allow ids < next_global_order_id + a small slack); the prefix cap delays legitimate cancels under a cancel storm, which is the intended trade-off.
ideas.why_new: s64 items cover FIFO selection and admission sizing for non-cancels; none examines that cancels are unvalidated, unpriced and prioritised.

ideas.title: Unauthenticated cancel priority lane lets ~80 KB/s of bogus cancels fill every block and starve all orders
ideas.area: torus-mempool native_pool.rs / lib.rs admission; torus-rpc torus.rs prescreen
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Cancels get three privileges with zero legitimacy check: (1) native_pool.rs:217 SortKey `(u8::from(!is_cancel), seq, sender, nonce)` sorts every cancel ahead of every non-cancel in selection (select_for_block_with_senders_excluding walks entries in that order, :337-380); (2) native_pool.rs:197-210 a cancel arriving at a full pool evicts the last non-cancel; (3) torus.rs:~432-440 and :1118-1130 the pool-full / admission-backlog pre-verify shed rejects non-cancels but lets cancels through to full verification. Admission (verify_one_action_with torus.rs:280-300, admit_gossip lib.rs:560-585, insert_with_restash_key native_pool.rs:171-235) checks only chain id, nonce window, batch size, known market and signature: nothing checks that CancelOrder{order_id} exists, is owned by the sender, or that the sender has any balance. Execution of an unknown id is a cheap miss (native_executor.rs:4972-4993 loops 10 books with get_order, then cancel_order → OrderNotFound) and no fee is charged. Fix: (a) at admission, for CancelOrder require the order to exist AND owner == sender via the node-local order store (book_reader::read_open_orders / get_order already used by torus_getOpenOrders, torus.rs:1516), plus a check against the sender's own pending PlaceOrders in the pool so fast cancels of not-yet-executed orders are not falsely rejected under CTE lag; for CancelAllOrders require ≥1 open order in that market; (b) bound the priority lane: at most N (e.g. 4) priority cancels per sender per block, the rest FIFO with everything else; (c) keep the pool-full eviction only for cancels that passed (a). Make sure in-progress item B (FIFO selection) does not carry the cancels-first byte over unchanged.
ideas.reasoning: Per-block per-sender cap is 64 (rate_limit.rs NATIVE_PER_BLOCK_CAP) and the pool per-sender cap is 512 (rate_limit.rs:167), so 4 fresh keys × 64 = 256 ≥ 200 = NATIVE_TOTAL_BLOCK_CAP fill the whole block. Sustaining it needs 200 cancels/block × 1.1 blk/s ≈ 220 signed CancelOrder JSONs/s ≈ 220 × ~350 B ≈ 77 KB/s and ~220 secp256k1 signs/s from the attacker; no funds, no session, no existing orders. Gossip (gossip_native_action) replicates them into every validator's pool, so every leader selects the same 200 no-op cancels first. Matched fills go from ~60-65k/s to 0 for as long as the attacker keeps nonces fresh (60 s window), while honest PlaceOrders are additionally shed pre-verify with 'pool full' once the pool fills. The exec-side cancels-only pacing tier (app.rs:5752, select_cancels_for_block) makes it worse under backlog: it selects only the attacker's prefix.

ideas.risk: An ownership check at admission reads exec state that lags commit under CTE; a cancel for an order placed one block earlier could be falsely rejected unless the pool's own pending PlaceOrders are consulted. A pure per-sender priority quota (b) has no such risk but still lets many keys consume the quota; (a)+(b) together are needed.

ideas.title: Any libp2p peer can write unverified action bodies durably to every validator (DA mirror before signature check) through an unbounded channel
ideas.area: torus-network swarm.rs native-action gossip/direct arms; torus-mempool lib.rs add_native_action_from_gossip; torus-node main.rs ingest task
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: The NATIVE_ACTION_TOPIC gossip arm (swarm.rs:1338-1400) has no sender check, no per-peer rate limit (TxGossipState is only used on the EVM TX_TOPIC else-branch at :1440) and no hash dedup; it bincode-decodes each action on the swarm thread and pushes into `native_action_inbound`, an UNBOUNDED mpsc (bridge.rs:218, swarm.rs:408-410). The direct-path pre-proposal marker (:1493-1505) does the same for any identify-registered peer (:1704-1712 registers non-validators) with up to MAX_DIRECT_MSG_SIZE = 8 MB per request (caps.rs:23). The consumer (main.rs:641-690) calls add_native_action_from_gossip, which at lib.rs:495 calls mirror_to_da BEFORE recovering/checking the claimed sender (:496-525), so every forged action is bincode-encoded and written to RocksDB CF_NATIVE_PENDING (native_da.rs:87-104) keyed by its hash; the oversize-batch guard (lib.rs:560-568) runs after the mirror; and per s64 #8 nothing ever removes these rows. Fix: (1) on the gossip-recover path move mirror_to_da after `verified_sender == claimed_sender` (keep the unconditional mirror only on the trusted push path, which is validator-authenticated); (2) drop native-action gossip/direct pushes from peers that are not validators or configured RPC nodes (is_validator_peer exists, swarm.rs:685); (3) make native_action_inbound a bounded channel with try_send + drop counter, like NativeGossipHandle (tx_gossip.rs:82-95); (4) apply TxGossipState's per-peer rate limit and 60 s hash dedup to NATIVE_ACTION_TOPIC too (it is already instantiated at swarm.rs:963).
ideas.reasoning: Cost to the attacker is bandwidth only; no valid signature is needed. Gossip: max_tx_message_size = 128 KB (config.rs:217); one peer at 10 MB/s = 80 msgs/s → 10 MB/s of forged bodies, and gossipsub (ValidationMode::Strict only checks the publisher's own libp2p signature, behaviour.rs:85) relays them to every validator, so each validator writes ~36 GB/hour into CF_NATIVE_PENDING + WAL with no eviction path. Direct: 8 MB per request with no rate limit is 60× more per message. Memory: the producer (swarm thread) decodes at wire rate while the consumer verifies at ecrecover/EIP-712 speed on half the cores; when in_flight ≥ 1024 the 'backpressure' (main.rs:664-672) only serializes the CONSUMER (ingest inline on one task), it never slows the producer, so the unbounded channel grows at wire rate: at 10 MB/s of decoded SignedNativeAction (heap size ≥ wire size) that is ~36 GB/hour of RSS on top of the existing 7.7 GB growth noted in s64 — an OOM within the hour. CPU: each forged action also costs a keccak + bincode + one failed ecrecover (~100 µs) or, for a batch, EIP-712 hashing of every order.

ideas.title: RPC: 64-connection cap with no per-IP limit is a zero-cost lockout, and single-submit verify bypasses the dedicated ingress pool
ideas.area: torus-rpc lib.rs server config; torus.rs submit_native_action
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: lib.rs:337-345 configures only max_connections (default 64) and max_response_body_size; jsonrpsee 0.26 defaults remain for max_request_body_size (10 MiB), batch_requests_config (Unlimited) and max_subscriptions_per_connection (1024) (jsonrpsee-server-0.26.0/src/server.rs:362-366). There is no per-IP/connection admission control anywhere (TxSubmitLimiter, lib.rs:151-190, is per recovered EVM sender). Separately, torus.rs:1140-1152 runs verify_one_action for the single endpoint on tokio::task::spawn_blocking (the 512-thread tokio blocking pool), while the batch endpoints run on the dedicated half-core ingress_verify_pool (torus.rs:348-362, 477-481) that was introduced precisely because shared-pool verify starved consensus (s352). Fix: (1) set max_request_body_size to 1-2 MiB, BatchRequestConfig::Limit(16-32), max_subscriptions_per_connection to ~32, and add a per-IP connection/token-bucket limit via jsonrpsee's HTTP middleware layer, then raise max_connections (env TORUS_RPC_MAX_CONNS already exists) behind it; (2) route submit_native_action through run_submit_pipeline / ingress_verify_pool so the 64 permits bound ingress to the dedicated pool for both endpoints.
ideas.reasoning: Lockout: 64 idle WebSocket connections from one host hold every slot; every honest client (bench generator, explorer, market makers) is refused. Cost: 64 TCP handshakes, zero CPU, indefinitely. CPU: with the single endpoint, 64 permits × one blocking thread each can run 64 concurrent verifies of PlaceOrderBatch(400) payloads carrying garbage signatures — every one pays JSON decode of ~80 KB + known-market lookups + EIP-712 hashing of 400 orders + one ecrecover before 'signature verification failed' (torus.rs:280-300; the code's own figure is ~70 ms CPU per bs500 action, torus.rs:477-479). At WAN-scale 12.5 MB/s (100 Mbit/s) that is ~156 verifies/s × ~50 ms ≈ 7.8 cores of an 18-core host shared by three validators and exec — the s352 mechanism (block time 529 → 4034 ms) via a pool the s352 fix does not cover. Subscriptions: 1024 per connection × 64 connections = 65k live sinks each buffering trade notifications.

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/jsonrpsee-server-0.26.0/src/server.rs:362-366 defaults: request 10 MiB, 1024 subs/conn, BatchRequestConfig::Unlimited

ideas.title: Non-validator peers can make the consensus thread serve full blocks (BlockDataRequest/ProposalRequest) and verify PCs (NewView) with no rate limit
ideas.area: torus-network swarm.rs direct arm + verify_sender_key; hotstuff_rs hotstuff/implementation.rs on_receive_msg dispatch
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: The /torus/direct arm (swarm.rs:1470-1560) gates only by ban list and verify_sender_key, which accepts any peer whose ed25519 key was registered at identify (swarm.rs:1704-1712, explicitly including non-validators); the ConsensusRateLimiter is applied only to the gossip arm (:1326), never to direct. handle_consensus_direct_traced (:3207-3240) decodes and enqueues into the algo thread's 10k-entry queue (:2840, :2984-2996). On the algo thread, on_receive_msg (implementation.rs:912-945) proposer-gates only Proposal/Nudge/ProposalHeader; the pacemaker validator-gates TimeoutVote/AdvanceView (pacemaker/implementation.rs:262-268, 466-469). Ungated for any origin: BlockDataRequest (implementation.rs:2174-2205: block_tree.block(hash) read + clone + send to origin, at ANY view since receiving.rs:269-271 passes block-data msgs unfiltered), ProposalRequest (:1612-1640: full Proposal sent to origin when view matches; the TC is not verified, only tc.high_tip.block_hash is read), and NewView (:1568-1585: highest_pc.is_correct = up to n ed25519 verifies, types.rs:149-170). Fix: (1) in handle_consensus_direct_traced (or the on_receive_msg dispatch) drop HotStuff/Pacemaker messages whose origin is not in the committed validator set (is_validator_peer at swarm.rs:685 / roles.rs:43 is_validator), keeping BlockSync serving for registered observers; (2) apply the existing ConsensusRateLimiter to the direct arm as well, with a low per-peer cap for BlockDataRequest/ProposalRequest (e.g. ≤ 10/s) so a compromised validator cannot do the same; (3) longer term, serve block-data requests from the network thread's store instead of the algo thread.
ideas.reasoning: Amplification: a BlockDataRequest is ~48 bytes of payload (chain_id, view, hash) plus the 32-byte sender key; the response is the full block, ~4 MB at cap 200 (s64 doc: '~4 MB durable body write'). That is ~50,000× outbound amplification per request, produced on the single hotstuff-algo thread (a 4 MB RocksDB get + clone + borsh encode ≈ 5-10 ms each, estimate). 100 requests/s from one peer (≈ 8 KB/s attacker bandwidth) costs the victim ~0.5-1 s of algo-thread time per second — the view (~650 ms) cannot complete — and 400 MB/s of egress, which also starves honest body dissemination. Block hashes are public (gossip headers). NewView with n garbage signatures costs ~3 × 60 µs ≈ 180 µs of algo-thread time per ~300 B message; ~5.5k msg/s (~1.7 MB/s) saturates the thread. The gossip arm's 50 msg/s per author limit is per libp2p PeerId, so it is also Sybil-able, but the direct path needs no Sybil at all.

ideas.title: Epoch validator-set updates are derived at vote time from exec-lagging local staking state (and written from the consensus thread)
ideas.area: torus-consensus app.rs epoch_validator_set_updates / torus-economics epoch.rs, staking.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Stop computing the epoch set from live `self.staking` inside `finish_validate`/`produce_block` (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:3944-4052, called at :4569 and :4721). Instead have the EXEC thread, when it applies a fixed lookback block (e.g. height H_epoch - epoch_length/2, or the last block of the previous epoch), compute `compute_new_validator_set` + rotation cap + minimum floor from the overlay it just applied and persist the resulting `ValidatorSet` (and its diff vs the current set) under a known key in the same atomic flush batch. 2) `epoch_validator_set_updates(H)` then only reads that persisted snapshot; if the snapshot height is not yet applied locally, wait for the exec pipeline (`pipeline_barrier`) rather than answer from stale state. 3) Move `apply_pending_rotations` (staking.rs:962-990) and `update_validator_statuses` (epoch.rs `update_validator_statuses`) out of the vote path into the exec of the boundary block (which is already a BARRIER, app.rs:1486-1495), so no consensus-thread write to CF_STAKING_VALIDATORS can race the exec overlay. 4) Add a 3-validator test with epoch_length small (e.g. 20) where a Delegate that changes the top-N lands in block H-1 and one node's exec is deliberately stalled 5 blocks before validate(H).
ideas.reasoning: `epoch_validator_set_updates` calls `EpochManager::compute_new_validator_set(&self.staking, ..)` which does `staking.all_validators()` = `iterate_cf(CF_STAKING_VALIDATORS)` on the node's DB (epoch.rs:35-48; staking.rs all_validators). Those rows are written by the EXEC thread when it applies Delegate/Undelegate/RegisterValidator/RotateValidatorKey (native_executor.rs:3141-3200 via ctx.staking). Under CTE the exec thread lags commit: sampler.csv for s65-votefix-ctl-r1 shows torus_exec_queue_depth peaking at 9 (val0) and 11 (val1, val2) blocks, and the header-first fast path validates H before H-1 is even committed (finish_validate comment, app.rs:4536-4560). hotstuff_rs stores whatever the App answered per node (`set_pending_validator_set_updates` internal.rs:1377, from block_tree insert) and never cross-checks it against other replicas. Failure scenario: epoch boundary at H; block H-1 holds a Delegate that pushes candidate X into the top-`max_validators`. Node A has applied H-1 when it validates H and answers `insert(X)`; node B has applied only H-4 and answers `None` (or the cached `Some((H, None))`, app.rs:3952-3953, which is never recomputed). After commit A's hotstuff validator set contains X and B's does not: quorum thresholds and leader schedule disagree, B rejects QCs carrying X's vote, A waits for X's vote; with n=3 any such split is below quorum and the chain halts. Second, weaker race: `apply_pending_rotations`/`update_validator_statuses` do `put_validator` directly into the DB from the consensus thread at vote time (app.rs:3958, :4002) while the exec overlay may hold a pending write for the same ValidatorState row (a Delegate in H-k not yet flushed); the later overlay flush overwrites the DB row on that node only ('each layer's writes override what sits below', backend.rs:1114-1135), so CF_STAKING_VALIDATORS (and any native root over it) differs between nodes. The devnet never exercises this: `epoch_length: 100_000` (torus-node/src/main.rs:305) vs ~330 blocks per 300 s cell.

ideas.title: Session expiry is never enforced on-chain: block path compares a seconds timestamp to a milliseconds expiry (July fix never landed on this line)
ideas.area: torus-types eip712.rs batch_verify / torus-consensus app.rs exec+validate callers / torus-bridge validator.rs, proposer.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Pass `torus_block.header.timestamp.saturating_mul(1000)` (ms) at the four block-path callers: crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1647-1649 (exec, batch_verify_native_actions_cached), app.rs:4492-4495 (validate_body_checks_core), crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:370 and proposer.rs:210 (resolve_sender). Optionally add the 120 s exec grace from the July fix (memory aeaf3a7059e3b906) inside batch_verify only, keep RPC strict. Fix the test at app.rs:11637 which encodes the ms-vs-seconds mismatch. This is a consensus validity change: deploy to all validators together.
ideas.reasoning: `exec_create_session` explicitly converts the block timestamp to ms and stores `expiry` in ms (native_executor.rs:5416-5457, MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS = 86_400_000). The verifier compares the raw `timestamp` argument against that ms value: eip712.rs:1143 `timestamp <= session.expiry` and :826 `current_timestamp > session.expiry`. Every block-path caller passes `header.timestamp`, which is `.as_secs()` (app.rs:4633-4636). 1.79e9 s is always below any ms expiry (>= 1.79e12), so no session ever expires at validate or exec. Only the RPC ingress uses ms (torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:486-499 `validate_with_sessions(current_time_ms)`), i.e. the 24 h cap is enforced solely by whichever node's RPC admitted the action. Failure scenario: a session key leaks; the owner relies on the 24 h expiry; an attacker submits through any leader whose admission path is bypassed (direct mempool insert, a modified node, or a leader whose clock is behind) and every honest validator accepts and executes the actions forever. Not a divergence today because all nodes make the same mistake, but memory shows the fix (`saturating_mul(1000)` + grace, branch perf/p3-throughput, July 2026) was proven red->green and never ported: `git log -S 'SESSION_EXPIRY_EXEC_GRACE_MS'` and `-S 'saturating_mul(1000)'` on app.rs return nothing on this line.

ideas.title: Liquidation/ADL driver iterates a HashMap of markets: order-dependent cross-margin outcomes would fork state the day it is wired in
ideas.area: torus-bridge native_executor.rs run_liquidation_checks / torus-core liquidation.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In `run_liquidation_checks` (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5733-5747) collect `ctx.margin_configs` into a Vec and `sort_by_key(|(id, _)| *id)` before the loop (same idiom as the A5 sort at :3757). Do the same in `LiquidationEngine::auto_deleverage` if it walks a map of positions, and make `results` push order follow market id. Add a unit test that runs the checks twice with two differently-seeded HashMaps (or two processes) and asserts identical post-state. While there, change `NativeExecContext.margin_configs`/`order_books` to BTreeMap or document that every iteration must be sorted (exec_cancel_all(None) at :5044 iterates `order_books.keys()` and is safe only because its margin sum is commutative and clamped once).
ideas.reasoning: `market_configs` is built by `ctx.margin_configs.iter()` (native_executor.rs:5740-5744); std HashMap order is randomised per process, so validators walk markets in different orders. Per market the code calls `check_liquidations` (reads ALL of a trader's positions across markets for the cross-margin check, liquidation.rs check_cross_liquidation), then `execute_liquidation` (mutates balances/positions) and `auto_deleverage` (mutates counterparties). For a trader with cross-margin positions in markets A and B near maintenance, node 1 processes A first: liquidating A frees/consumes collateral so B passes (or fails) the check; node 2 processes B first and reaches the opposite outcome. Positions, balances and ADL victims then differ across nodes, i.e. a native-state fork on the first such block. Today there is no caller of `run_liquidation_checks` or `aggregate_oracle_prices` anywhere in crates/*/src (only the definitions), so nothing diverges yet, which is exactly why it will not be caught by the current devnet.

ideas.title: Block header timestamp is leader wall-clock with no monotonic or bound check at validate; one skewed clock breaks session creation for 1/3 of blocks
ideas.area: torus-consensus app.rs produce_block / finish_validate, torus-bridge native_executor.rs session gates
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In `finish_validate` (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4536-4560), when `last_header` is the parent, reject `header.timestamp < last_header.timestamp` (deterministic), and reject `header.timestamp > local_now + MAX_FUTURE_DRIFT` (e.g. 30 s, a vote-only rule as in Ethereum's block validity). In `produce_block` (:4633) clamp the timestamp to `max(now, parent.timestamp)`. Add a test with a leader whose timestamp is +2 h and assert that CreateSession in its block is not rejected as 'already expired'.
ideas.reasoning: `produce_block` sets `timestamp = SystemTime::now().as_secs()` (app.rs:4633-4636) and the header is signed via canonical_header_bytes (torus-types lib.rs:431-438). validate_datum_after_fail_stop / validate_body_checks_core / finish_validate check hash binding, decode, signatures and parent_hash only; there is no comparison of header.timestamp against the parent or the local clock anywhere in app.rs or torus-bridge. Execution trusts it: exec_create_session rejects with 'session already expired' when `expiry <= ts*1000` and 'expiry exceeds 24h maximum' when `expiry > ts*1000 + 86_400_000` (native_executor.rs:5416-5421), and after finding 2 is fixed every session-signed action is validated against it. Failure scenario on the 3-validator round robin: validator C's NTP is off by +2 h. Every third block carries a +2 h timestamp; a user who creates a session with expiry = now + 1 h (bench tools use now_ms + 1 h, memory aeaf3a70) is rejected 'already expired' whenever C is leader, the nonce is consumed and the client sees a 33% random failure rate. With a -25 h clock every CreateSession in C's blocks fails 'exceeds 24h'. Once expiry is enforced (finding 2), a +25 h leader makes all session actions in its proposals invalid at validate, so all nodes reject its blocks and each of its views times out, i.e. a single misconfigured clock adds ~1 timeout per 3 views to the 120-170 per 300 s already measured. Timestamps can also go backwards between consecutive blocks, which oracle submissions (submit_price(..., ctx.timestamp), :5526) and order timestamps (:4816) record verbatim.

ideas.title: torus_getOpenOrders scans the whole per-market (or whole-node) order-row store per call; the trader index CF is dead
ideas.area: torus-rpc torus.rs get_open_orders / torus-core book_reader.rs read_open_orders / precompiles.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Maintain a trader-keyed secondary index of resting orders. The key layout already exists and is unused: CF_NATIVE_ORDERS = trader(20)+market(8)+order_id(16) (precompiles.rs:1407-1421 `write_stored_order`, which has zero callers in any crate). Write/delete it in the deferred book-save pass on the flush worker (exec_pipeline.rs `apply_deferred_book_save`) so it lands in the same atomic batch as the book rows; or, cheaper, keep it in CF_BOOK_ORDER_ROWS under a second key tag `trader ‖ market ‖ order_id` so it is node-local like the rows themselves. 2) Change `read_open_orders` (book_reader.rs:448-560) to prefix-iterate that index and fetch at most `limit` rows, instead of `iterate_optional_cf(CF_BOOK_ORDER_ROWS, market prefix / None)` which materialises every row of the market (or of all markets) into a Vec<(Vec<u8>,Vec<u8>)> and decodes each one before filtering by trader and truncating to `limit`. 3) Until then, wrap the handler body in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` and require `market_id` (reject the all-markets form) so a single call cannot pin one of the 4 rpc-worker threads (main.rs:944-945) for seconds. 4) Fix the EVM precompile `getOpenOrders(address,bytes32)` (precompiles.rs:340, 468-478): it reads CF_NATIVE_ORDERS, which nothing writes, so it always returns empty arrays; point it at the same index.
ideas.reasoning: In the bench configuration (TORUS_BOOK_ROWS=3 -> BookLayout::LevelAuthority, book_reader.rs:62-71) `read_open_orders` takes the `LevelAuthority` branch (book_reader.rs:497-556): `iterate_optional_cf(state, CF_BOOK_ORDER_ROWS, Some(market))` for one market, or `iterate_optional_cf(.., None)` plus a full CF_NATIVE_ORDER_BOOKS pass for all markets. `StateDb::iterate_cf` (backend.rs:116-146) copies every key and value into owned Vecs. At the end of s65-votefix-ctl-r1 the resident books hold torus_exec_resting_orders = 3,090,909 orders (sampler.csv last rows), i.e. ~309k per market. So one `torus_getOpenOrders(trader, market)` touches 309k rows and one `torus_getOpenOrders(trader)` touches 3.09M rows, each row costing two heap allocations (25-byte key + ~90-byte value) and a `decode_order_row` + `check_row_id`, before `out.truncate(limit)` at :558. Assuming ~1-2 us per row (RocksDB iteration from block cache + 2 allocs + borsh decode) that is ~0.3-0.6 s per single-market call and ~3-6 s per all-markets call, with ~400-600 MB of transient allocation for the latter (3.09M x (~115 B payload + 48 B of Vec headers)). The handler is an `async fn` that does this inline on the RPC tokio runtime (no spawn_blocking), which has only 4 workers (main.rs:944-945); four concurrent open-order queries stall every other RPC call on the node, including `submitNativeActions`, for the duration. A trader polling open orders to learn whether an order filled therefore sees multi-second query latency that grows linearly with book depth, and the polling itself degrades submit latency for everyone. The EVM precompile path returns an empty list unconditionally because its CF is never populated.

ideas.title: Trade-history writer falls behind under load and never catches up: user-visible trade history lags 60-95 s and the 256-batch cap will stall execution on runs longer than ~15 min
ideas.area: torus-state bg_writer.rs / torus-consensus app.rs trade_writer hand-off / RPC getUserTrades, getBlockTrades, getTradeHistory, newTrades
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Add `torus_trade_writer_queued_batches` (val0 max and end-of-drain value) to the harness headline and make the drain gate require it to return to 0; today the cell is declared 'drained' while 55-102 blocks of trade rows are still queued. 2) A/B the writer policy on this line: `TORUS_BG_WRITER_LOW_PRI=0` (bg_writer.rs:142-147, default ON) and WAL-off for CF_NATIVE_TRADES / CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES; measure the queue trajectory, not just matched/s. 3) If the writer still drains slower than ~1.1 native blocks/s at ~174k rows/block, size a real fix: either fold the trade rows into the flush worker's atomic batch (exec_pipeline.rs run_job, so history is never behind state) or give this writer its own RocksDB instance so the write controller's low-pri delay cannot pin it. 4) Expose the writer lag (blocks) on the RPC side so trade-history responses can carry a 'complete through height h' field instead of silently omitting recent fills.
ideas.reasoning: Each native block hands one packed batch of trade rows to `torus-trade-writer` (app.rs:2136-2150, `send_packed`), a `sync_channel(256)` (app.rs:3262-3266) written in 2048-row low_pri chunks (bg_writer.rs:24-32, 128-131). At 58,118 fills per native block (ctl-r1 headline) with three rows per fill (primary, maker, taker; packed-trade-history doc) that is ~174k rows = ~85 write groups per block. The sampler shows the queue rising monotonically once fills per block grow: val0 in ctl-r1 goes 0 -> 13 (t=181 s) -> 45 (t=281 s) -> 57 (t=302 s, load end) -> 66 (t=342 s, end of the 49 s drain, still rising); ctl-r2 ends at 102, ctl-r3 at 73, fix-r1 at 55, all still non-zero when the harness declares the cell drained. Between t=181 and t=281 the queue grows 0.32 batches/s while native blocks arrive at 1.09/s, so the writer drains only ~0.77 blocks of rows per second. User-visible effect: `torus_getUserTrades` (torus.rs:1674-1748, reads CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES), `getBlockTrades`, `getTradeHistory` and the newTrades scan (lib.rs:485-560) all read these CFs, so a fill that executed at height H is not queryable until the writer reaches H: 66-102 queued blocks x ~0.92 s per native block = 60-95 s of history lag at the end of a 5-minute cell, growing linearly. Failure scenario: at +0.32 batches/s the 256 slot cap is reached after another (256-102)/0.32 = ~480 s, i.e. ~13 minutes of sustained load. Then `send_packed` blocks the execution thread until a slot frees (bg_writer.rs:192-194, 'a full queue makes send block'), so exec throughput drops to the writer's ~0.7-0.8 blk/s; the 64-slot exec channel (app.rs:3324-3325) then fills at (1.09-0.77) blk/s in ~200 s, after which the HotStuff thread parks on the blocking exec send, the scenario app.rs:5093-5097 describes as a 'view-timeout cascade'. matched/s would fall to ~70 % of today's and the chain could stop committing.

ideas.title: No status or receipt for native actions: a trader cannot learn whether a submitted action was included, executed, dropped at exec, or silently expired, and cannot tell which height the state they read reflects
ideas.area: torus-rpc torus.rs submit/query surface, torus-consensus app.rs commit and exec paths, torus-state cf.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Add a node-local `CF_NATIVE_ACTION_STATUS` keyed by action hash (the hash `submitNativeAction` already returns, torus.rs:557). Write `Included{height}` in `on_committed_block` from the CompactBlock's `native_action_hashes` (app.rs ~5080 already collects them), and `Applied{height, per-order results}` / `Dropped{reason}` on the exec thread next to the existing replay-guard and FIX-2 drop points (app.rs:1725-1749) and the `orders_rejected_book` counter (native_executor.rs:4612). Route the writes through the same background writer as trade rows or through W's batch. 2) Add `torus_getActionStatus(hash)` that answers `pending` (via the existing but RPC-unused `NativePool::get_by_hash`, native_pool.rs:87), `included`, `applied`, `dropped`, or `unknown/expired`. 3) Add `torus_getAppliedHeight` (or a field on `torus_getLeader`/block responses) exposing META_NATIVE_APPLIED_HEIGHT / `FlushWorker::durable_height` (exec_pipeline.rs:229) so clients can do read-your-writes: poll until applied >= included height before trusting getPosition/getBalances/getOpenOrders. 4) Return a distinct error at admission-time expiry (`NonceTooOld`) and count pool-side `evict_expired` per sender so the 'silent' path at least becomes observable; optionally reject at submit when the pool's admission horizon already exceeds the remaining nonce window.
ideas.reasoning: Today the only artefact a client gets is the action hash (torus.rs:538-560). Nothing consumes that hash afterwards: the `torus` namespace (torus.rs:90-230) has no status/receipt method, `CF_RECEIPTS` and `CF_TX_HASH_TO_LOCATION` are EVM-only (eth.rs:680-770), and `NativePool::get_by_hash` is called only by tests. Three outcomes are therefore invisible: (a) pool expiry — `evict_expired` (native_pool.rs:451-467) removes entries with no log or per-sender counter; in ctl-r1 35,309 of 107,294 submitted actions (33 %) went this way; (b) exec-time drops — FIX-2 signature/session drops and replay skips are `tracing::warn!` lines (app.rs:1725-1749), and book-rejected orders are only `orders_rejected_book` (17,448 per cell); (c) execution lag — the exec channel sits at a mean depth of 1.9-3.2 blocks and up to 6-11 in the load window (sampler `torus_exec_queue_depth`), so the state a `getPosition`/`getOpenOrders` call reads is 1.4-8 s behind the height `eth_blockNumber` reports (known bug 6), and there is no applied-height signal for a client to wait on. The practical consequence for a trader: after submitting, the fastest 'did it fill' signal is trade history, which lags 60-95 s under load (previous finding) and never shows expired or rejected orders; open orders cannot distinguish 'filled' from 'expired' from 'rejected' because in all three cases the order is simply absent. A status CF written at commit and at exec bounds time-to-know at the exec lag (~1.5-3 s mean) and an explicit applied height turns 'read something' into 'read my write'.

ideas.title: newTrades WebSocket fan-out cannot survive load once the known scan-timing bug is fixed: one message per fill, 256-block retention, and a slow subscriber is silently disconnected on Lagged
ideas.area: torus-rpc torus.rs subscribe(newTrades) / lib.rs BlockNotifier / torus-node main.rs on_commit_block
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) In `subscribe` (torus.rs:1774-1812) send one `SubscriptionMessage` per (block, market) carrying an array of trades instead of one per trade, and pre-serialise once per block for all subscribers. 2) Replace `while let Ok(trades) = rx.recv().await` with an explicit match: on `RecvError::Lagged(n)` emit a `{resyncFromHeight: h}` notice and continue, instead of returning (which drops the sink and closes the subscription with no error payload). 3) Skip `scan_trades_for_block` in the commit handler (main.rs:889-890) when `new_trades.receiver_count() == 0`, and shrink the broadcast buffer from 256 whole-block Vec<Value>s (lib.rs:118) to a few blocks, storing an `Arc<[u8]>` of the serialised payload rather than 58k `serde_json::Value`s. 4) Do this together with the bug-6 fix (scan after exec, per `event.block`), because that fix is what makes the per-block payload real.
ideas.reasoning: With the bug-6 fix in place, every native block would deliver its full fill set: 58,118 fills per native block (ctl-r1 headline) at 1.09 blocks/s. The current subscriber loop sends one WebSocket message per fill (torus.rs:1789-1806), so a single subscriber receives ~58k messages per block, ~63k messages/s, each ~250 B of JSON = ~14-16 MB/s per subscriber, on the 4-thread RPC runtime; `sink.send(msg).await` applies per-connection back-pressure, so a subscriber that cannot absorb a block in <0.92 s falls behind. The broadcast channel then retains up to 256 blocks of `Vec<serde_json::Value>` for that receiver: 256 x 58k x ~400 B per Value object (7 String fields) ~= 5.9 GB of node heap for one slow client before tokio reports `Lagged`. When it does, the `while let Ok` loop exits, the task returns, the `SubscriptionSink` is dropped and the client's stream ends with no explanation; it has no way to know which heights it missed. Today this is masked only because the handler scans CF_NATIVE_TRADES at commit time, before execution and the trade writer have produced the rows (bug 6), so most scans are empty; the 30 % of heights that are notified twice already show the double-delivery symptom. Independently, `scan_trades_for_block` runs on every commit regardless of subscriber count (main.rs:889), building 58k JSON objects per block for nobody once history is present.
